requests.user: {"question":"apa gagasan utama buku ini?","book":"Discourses","examinedBefore":640,"totalWindows":957,"previousNotes":[{"text":"Tesis utama buku: hanya penggunaan yang benar atas penampakan (right use of appearances) yang berada dalam kuasa kita; fakultas rasional adalah satu-satunya yang dapat mengkontemplasi dirinya sendiri dan menilai fakultas lain. Segala hal lain (tubuh, harta, orang tercinta) di luar kuasa kita; manusia menderita karena terikat pada banyak hal eksternal.","source_ids":["S3","S5","S6"]},{"text":"Kunci ketenangan: selalu membedakan apa milikku dan bukan milikku. Kematian, penjara, pengasingan harus dihadapi tanpa ratapan — tubuh bisa dibelenggu, tetapi kemauan (will) tidak bisa ditaklukkan bahkan oleh Zeus. Contoh: Lateranus mengulurkan leher dengan tenang; Agrippinus tetap makan setelah dijatuhi hukuman pengasingan.","source_ids":["S9","S11","S12"]},{"text":"Menjaga karakter (proper character): yang rasional selalu diterima, yang irasional tak tertanggungkan — karena itu kita butuh disiplin. Agrippinus menolak ikut tontonan Nero: ia ingin menjadi 'ungu' pada jubah, bukan sekadar satu benang biasa; Priscus Helvidius tetap bersuara di senat meski Vespasian mengancam mati — tugas kaisar membunuh, tugasnya mati tanpa takut.","source_ids":["S15","S18","S19"]},{"text":"Allah adalah bapa semua manusia: manusia memiliki kekerabatan ganda — tubuh bersama hewan, nalar bersama dewa. Yang banyak condong pada daging dan menjadi seperti serigala, singa, atau rubah; sebagian kecil yang mengenali asal ilahiah tidak memiliki pikiran rendah tentang dirinya.","source_ids":["S27","S29"]},{"text":"Kemajuan (progres) bukan menguasai banyak buku filsafat, tetapi melatih desire dan aversion agar tidak gagal memperoleh yang diinginkan atau jatuh pada yang dihindari; bukti kemajuan adalah keadaan kemauan yang bebas, setia, dan sederhana dalam tindakan sehari-hari. Tragedi adalah gambaran gejolak orang yang menghargai hal eksternal.","source_ids":["S32","S36","S37"]},{"text":"Gagasan utama: manusia adalah makhluk rasional, kerabat/kepunyaan Tuhan; tujuan hidup adalah menggunakan akal dengan benar — memahami penggunaan penampakan, bukan sekadar memakainya seperti hewan. Alam berakhir pada kontemplasi dan hidup sesuai alam; memulai dan berakhir seperti hewan adalah memalukan.","source_ids":["S48","S49"]},{"text":"Providence: dari segala yang ada dan terjadi mudah memuji providensi bila memiliki dua hal — kemampuan melihat kegunaan segala hal dan watak bersyukur. Kesesuaian struktur dunia (mata, cahaya, warna) membuktikan Sang Pencipta.","source_ids":["S46","S47"]},{"text":"Kesulitan hidup adalah sarana latihan kebajikan: seperti Hercules membutuhkan singa dan hydra, manusia diberi kebesaran jiwa, keberanian, dan ketahanan untuk menanggung apa pun yang terjadi; mengeluh dan menyalahkan dewa adalah kekufuran akibat jiwa yang hina.","source_ids":["S52","S53"]},{"text":"Kekerasan kepalaan (menolak kebenaran yang jelas) ada dua macam: pada akal dan pada rasa malu. Orang yang melihat kontradiksi tetapi tidak berubah lebih buruk dari orang yang tidak melihat — akalnya tidak hilang melainkan dibinatangkan; itu bukan kekuatan budi.","source_ids":["S42","S43"]},{"text":"Logika dan argumen dialektis adalah kewajiban hidup: cukup tidak hanya mengetahui prinsip membedakan benar-salah, tetapi harus ada kemahiran seperti membedakan drachma asli-palsu. Namun bila premis berubah makna, kita boleh menarik persetujuan dari konsekuensinya.","source_ids":["S57","S60"]},{"text":"Kerabat dengan Tuhan: jangan menyebut diri warga Athena melainkan warga dunia (kosmopolites); komunitas tertinggi adalah manusia dan Tuhan. Contoh Socrates yang memilih mati daripada meninggalkan tugas yang Tuhan tempatkan; tubuh dan harta bukan kekuatan tiran atas kita.","source_ids":["S72","S78"]},{"text":"Gagasan utama: manusia berkerabat dengan Tuhan sehingga memiliki dari dalam dirinya sendiri hal-hal terpenting (kemuliaan jiwa); orang penakut dan hina hanyalah 'mayat dan segayung darah', dan tidak ada orang yang membuat orang lain sengsara—yang benar-benar berharga tidak diperoleh dari orang lain (tanah, uang, jabatan).","source_ids":["S81"]},{"text":"Epictetus mengkritik mereka yang mengejar jabatan di Roma: orang tua yang bersumpah akan hidup tenang setelah pengasingan langsung melupakan segalanya begitu menerima surat dari Caesar. Manusia memang dibuat untuk bekerja, tetapi pekerjaan yang benar adalah mempelajari administrasi dunia dan siapa diri kita, bukan urusan biji gandum dan tanah.","source_ids":["S84","S86"]},{"text":"Dialog tentang kasih sayang alami: meninggalkan anak yang sakit bukanlah tindakan penyayang—kasih sayang harus konsisten dengan rasio; yang keduanya penyayang dan rasional itulah yang benar dan baik. Kita butuh kriteria (bukan sekadar 'semua orang melakukannya') untuk menilai baik-buruk, seperti penglihatan untuk warna.","source_ids":["S92","S93","S94"]},{"text":"Sebab segala tindakan adalah will/opini (dogma) kita sendiri, bukan hal luar: bukan kematian Patroklus yang membuat Achilles meratap, tetapi pilihannya. Kematian, pengasingan, atau rasa sakit tidak menyebabkan kita berbuat apa pun; kita harus membuang opini salah seperti membuang tumor, dan hanya memeriksa opini, bukan tanah, budak, atau kuda.","source_ids":["S96","S97","S98"]},{"text":"Kebahagiaan (contentment): manusia harus meneliti pendapat tentang para dewa lalu menundukkan pikirannya kepada Yang mengatur semuanya seperti warga yang taat pada hukum. Kebebasan adalah belajar menginginkan segala sesuatu terjadi sebagaimana terjadi; yang tidak menerima hukumannya adalah menjadi dirinya sendiri—di mana ia berada dengan tidak rela, di situ ia dipenjara (Socrates tidak dipenjara karena ada dengan rela).","source_ids":["S103","S104","S107"]},{"text":"Tuhan mengawasi segala hal: jiwa kita adalah bagian dan potongan dari Tuhan, dan setiap manusia diberi penjaga (daimon) yang tidak pernah tidur; kita harus bersumpah kepada Tuhan—tidak pernah membangkang, tidak mencela apa yang diberikan, dan tidak dengan enggan melakukan atau menderita apa yang perlu—sumpah yang menghormati diri sendiri, bukan Caesar.","source_ids":["S115","S117","S118"]},{"text":"Filosofi tidak menjanjikan hal eksternal apa pun; materinya adalah hidup orang itu sendiri. Angka saudara marah bukan wilayahnya — ia hanya menjamin bagian penguasa (governing part) selalu sesuai alam. Kebenaran besar tidak terbentuk tiba-tiba, seperti buah ara butuh waktu matang.","source_ids":["S121","S123"]},{"text":"Providence terlihat bahkan dalam hal kecil: susu dari rumput, keju dari susu, rambut dagu sebagai tanda pembeda pria-wanita. Hymn kepada Tuhan harus dinyanyikan terus — Epictetus menyebut dirinya makhluk rasional yang tugasnya memuji Tuhan; 'jika aku burungNightangle aku menyanyi seperti nightangle, tetapi aku makhluk rasional, maka aku memuji Tuhan.'","source_ids":["S127","S128","S129"]},{"text":"Seni logis diperlukan karena akal menganalisis fakultas lain dan harus menganalisis dirinya sendiri; tanpa kriteria (seperti modius untuk gandum) tidak ada pengukuran akurat. Kita tidak butuh Chrysippus karena dirinya, tetapi untuk memahami kehendak alam.","source_ids":["S133","S136"]},{"text":"Kebebasan will terbukti: tak ada yang bisa memaksa assent pada yang palsu atau menghalangi assent pada yang benar. Yang memaksa bukan yang diletakkan di depan (ketakutan akan mati), melainkan opini kita sendiri — will memaksa will. Jika memilih, kita bebas, tidak menyalahkan siapa pun; segala jadi sesuai kehendak kita dan Tuhan.","source_ids":["S137","S138"]},{"text":"Jangan marah pada kesalahan orang lain: pelaku salah adalah yang keliru tentang baik-buruk, seperti buta — layak dikasihani bukan dibenci. Kita marah karena menghargai hal yang dicuri; jangan menghargai pakaian, tak akan marah pada pencuri. Latih diri dari hal kecil (sakit kepala tanpa 'alas!') menuju yang besar.","source_ids":["S141","S143","S145"]},{"text":"Tiran hanya menguasai tubuh (kaki, leher), tidak akan (will). Yang membuat orang takut bukan tiran dan pengawalnya, melainkan opini sendiri. Manusia yang ditunjuk Caesar jadi tukang sepatunya langsung tampak bijak di mata orang — nilai yang salah. Bakat dirinya mencakup memikirkan diri sendiri, dan karena manusia rasional tak bisa memperoleh kepentingannya sendiri tanpa berkontribusi pada kepentingan bersama, mementingkan diri tidak kontrasosial.","source_ids":["S151","S152","S154"]},{"text":"Akal sendiri berasal dari penampakan (system of appearances) sehingga bisa mengkhawati dirinya sendiri; tugas pertama filosof adalah memeriksa penampakan tanpa menerima tanpa ujian. Doktrin filosof sangat singkat: tujuan manusia mengikuti para dewa, dan baik adalah penggunaan penampakan yang tepat; kata-kata panjang hanya perlu menjelaskan apa Tuhan, penampakan, dan alam.","source_ids":["S158","S160"]},{"text":"Kritik terhadap Epicurus: kendati mengakui manusia bersifat sosial, ia menempatkan kebaikan pada 'kulitnya' sehingga menyarankan orang bijak tidak membesarkan anak—padahal begitu anak lahir, sayang padanya di luar kuasa kita; bahkan domba dan serigala tidak meninggalkan anaknya. Orang bijak seharusnya terlibat urusan publik, bukan memperlakukan manusia seperti sekawanan lalat.","source_ids":["S174","S175"]},{"text":"Kesulitan adalah lawan sparring dari Tuhan: seperti pelatih gulat mencocokkan kita dengan pemuda tangguh agar menjadi juara Olimpiade. Diogenes adalah penembak ronda teladan—melaporkan kematian bukan jahat, ketenaran gemuruh orang gila, hidup telanjang dan tidur di tanah lebih baik, dengan bukti ketenangan dan kebebasannya sendiri; penembak ronda penakut yang lapor musuh dekat hanya layak disuruh pulang.","source_ids":["S178","S179"]},{"text":"Hidup seperti berperan: manusia hanya boleh membawa yang miliknya (kirimannya), bukan kemudi atau dayung kapal—hal luar boleh dicabut satu per satu (toga, tubuh) tanpa takut. Harta seperti tempat tidur di penginapan; tragedi hanya terjadi pada orang kaya dan raja, orang miskin tidak punya peran tragis; bila permainan tidak menyenangkan, 'aku tidak bermain lagi'—pintu terbuka.","source_ids":["S180","S181","S182"]},{"text":"Perintah Zeus sudah cukup: jaga apa milikmu (integritas, rasa malu yang baik), jangan menginginkan milik orang lain; bila memegangnya tidak perlu arahan lain. Hidup itu permainan Saturnalia: patuh raja yang ditunjuk agar permainan tidak kacau, tetapi tidak ada yang memaksa kita berpikir menderita—seperti hipotesis logika, boleh menyanggupi 'sial', tetapi Zeus melarang menganggap diri hina.","source_ids":["S186","S187","S188"]},{"text":"Kita yang menghimpit diri sendiri lewat opini: ingin duduk di tempat senator menghimpit; hinaan hanya efektif lewat kelemahan orang yang dihinakan—jika mendengar seperti batu, tidak ada untungnya. Yang dijaga itulah yang diserang: bila menaruh hormat pada tubuh atau harta kecil, di situlah kita jadi budak. Socrates selalu satu wajah karena mempraktikkan kebebasan tanpa hambatan.","source_ids":["S189","S190","S191","S192"]},{"text":"Hukum hidup mendahului hukum hipotesis logis: bertindak sesuai alam adalah hukum dasar; filsuf melatih teori dulu (lebih mudah) baru urusan hidup yang lebih sulit. Awal filsafat adalah menyadari kelemahan fakultas penuntun—yang tak bisa menelan sepotong pun membeli seluruh jilid lalu memuntahkannya; orang membaca argumen hipotetis hanya untuk dipuji orang senatori (contoh: pengeluh punya 1,5 juta denarii yang membuat Epaphroditus tercengang, bukan mentertawakan).","source_ids":["S195","S196","S199"]},{"text":"Empat cara penampakan muncul; tugas orang terdidik menilai dengan benar. Ramuan melawan kebiasaan adalah kebiasaan yang berlawanan; melawan penampakan menipu adalah prekognisi yang bersih; melawan kematian—ia perlu dan bukan kejahatan, jadi tanpa rasa takut. Ketiadaan kesalehan lahir karena piety dan kepentingan pribadi dianggap terpisah.","source_ids":["S202","S205"]},{"text":"Jangan marah kepada orang lain: jiwa hanya menyetujui yang tampak benar (Plato: jiwa kehilangan kebenaran dengan tak rela); Medea terlilit karena mengira balas dendam lebih menguntungkan. Orang sesat pada fakultas tertinggi patut dikasihani seperti orang buta, bukan dibenci. Segala tindakan diukur oleh penampakan.","source_ids":["S210","S212","S213"]},{"text":"Iliad hanyalah penampakan dan penggunaannya: pembakaran Troya tidak lebih dahsyat dari sarang bangau yang terbakar—bedanya manusia memiliki kejujuran, kemoderatan, kesetiaan, kecerdasan. Kehancuran sejati adalah kehancuran opini benar: Alexander hancur saat kehilangan karakter, Achilles saat marah dan lupa tugasnya.","source_ids":["S214","S216","S217"]},{"text":"Esensi Baik adalah kemauan; hal luar hanya bahan bagi kemauan. Hukum Allah: ambil kebaikan dari dirimu sendiri. Tirani hanya mengancam tubuh; tidak ada yang lebih kuat daripada kemauan kecuali kemauan sendiri—sepuluh orang lebih kuat dalam mengekang, tetapi tidak dalam opini yang benar.","source_ids":["S222","S224"]},{"text":"Socrates menafsir ulang: yang dibawa ke penjara hanyalah 'tubuh miskinnya'; 'Anytus dan Melitus dapat membunuhku, tetapi tidak menyakitiku.' Kesulitan adalah ujian pembelajaran: seperti atlet yang ingin lawan berat, orang terdidik harus menunjukkan ajarannya dalam praktik, bukan argumen kecil di sudut sekolah; jadilah saksi Allah bahwa yang eksternal bukan baik atau jahat.","source_ids":["S226","S232","S235"]},{"text":"Pelayan yang baik menghormati semua orang sesuai 'relasi': ayah, saudara, keabadian—mengingat bahwa adalah watak dewata mempertahankan diri dari mimpi dan kecenderungan; putusan orang yang belum terdidik tentang kesalehan tidak lebih penting daripada seorang musisi yang salah menilai tali lyre. Hamba yang lari menikmati teater dengan ketakutan; membebaskan diri dari 'majikan' (kematian, kesenangan, sakit) menghapus seluruh ketakutan.","source_ids":["S236","S238","S239"]},{"text":"Sikap yang harus disiapkan dalam kesulitan: saat menghadapi orang besar, ingat ada yang melihat dari atas; pengasingan, penjara, mati, aib tetap hal indiferen yang tak berubah — hanya hal di luar kemauan yang 'tak ada bagiku'; Baik adalah kemauan sebagaimana mestinya dan penggunaan penampakan; tujuan hidup adalah mengikuti Tuhan. YAng begitu belajar akan berani karena tahu semua persiapan gelar-gelar kuasa 'bukanlah apa-apa'.","source_ids":["S243","S244"]},{"text":"Percaya diri dan kehati-hatian tidak bertentangan bila diterapkan pada objek berbeda: kehati-hatian pada hal dalam kemauan (satu-satunya jahat), keberanian pada hal di luar kemauan. Manusia terbalik seperti rusa yang takut pada bulu pemburu lalu lari ke jaring: takut pada kematian, sakit, aib (hal luar) tetapi gegabah pada tipu, nafsu, aib tindakan (hal will). Bukan kematian yang menakutkan, melainkan ketakutan pada kematian.","source_ids":["S247","S248","S249"]},{"text":"Kematian dan sakit adalah 'topeng tragedi': putar dan periksa — tidak menggigit; pintu selalu terbuka bila tak tertahankan. Kebebasan sejati adalah milik yang terdidik: hidup tanpa kesalahan, takut, duka, dan gejolak adalah bebas; budak yang dibebaskan di pengadilan tetap tak bebas bila uang, kekasih, atau tiran jadi majikannya. Socrates menulis untuk menguji dirinya sendiri dalam praktik, bukan karya-karya kosong; pamer sejati pemuda terdidik adalah 'sajikan kematian, penjara, siksaan — aku tak kecewa dan tak jatuh'.","source_ids":["S252","S254","S257","S258"]},{"text":"Ketenangan dalam perkara (contoh: ke pengadilan): bila tujuannya mempertahankan will sesuai alam, aman penuh — tak ada yang menguasainya; bila ingin mempertahankan hal luar, siaplah jadi budak penuh (berlutut, menangis). Socrates seumur hidup bersiap menghadapi sidang karena tak pernah berbuat zalim. Minta 'saran untuk setiap kejadian' seperti orang buta huruf minta tahu nama apa yang akan ditulis; latihan membuat siap untuk semua, dan yang mengejar hal luar pasti terombang-ambing pada kehendak majikannya.","source_ids":["S262","S263","S264","S267"]},{"text":"Magnanimitas konsisten dengan kehati-hatian lewat analogi meja judi: keping dan dadanya indiferen, tetapi penggunaan lemparan harus cermat — hal luar tak milik kita, will milik kita; gunakan hal luar dengan hati-hati karena penggunaannya bukan indiferen, sambil tetap tenang karena materinya indiferen. Seperti pelayaran: pilih kapten, pelaut, waktu; datang badai, tugas kita selesai — bila kapal tenggelam, lakukan satu-satunya yang bisa: tidak tenggelam.","source_ids":["S279","S280"]},{"text":"Manusia dibentuk untuk kesetiaan (fidelity); perusaknya meruntuhkan ciri khas manusia: kesopanan, kesucian, hubungan tetangga, persahabatan, komunitas — jadilah serigala atau kera, dan layak dibuang seperti peralatan rusak ke tumpukan kotoran. Argumen 'wanita memang bersifat umum secara alam' dibantah dengan analogi: babi dan teater juga umum bagi semua, tetapi setelah dibagikan, mencuri porsi orang lain adalah perampokan.","source_ids":["S274","S276"]},{"text":"Metafora permainan bola: keahlian ada pada melempar dan menangkap, bukan pada bola itu sendiri — bola (hal eksternal) harus dianggap tak berharga. Socrates bermain bola di pengadilannya: omongannya yang menyenangkan pada Anytus adalah lemparan; bolanya adalah hidup, belenggu, racun. Kita harus mengerahkan seluruh keahlian pada materi eksternal tanpa menghargai materinya, seperti tukang tenun yang mengerjakan wol apa pun yang diterimanya.","source_ids":["S282","S283"]},{"text":"Foot analogy: manusia adalah bagian dari keseluruhan, bukan makhluk terpisah — kaki yang menjejak lumpur atau dipotong demi tubuh masih sesuai alam sebagai kaki; manusia yang sakit, miskin, atau mati muda tetap sesuai alam sebagai bagian dari negara yang pertama (dewa dan manusia). Hidup seperti satu jam dalam sehari: hadir lalu lewat; bagaimana cara berlalunya tak penting.","source_ids":["S281","S285"]},{"text":"Hal indiferen vs penilaiannya: proposisi hipotetis indiferen, tetapi penilaian tentangnya tidak (pengetahuan, opini, atau kekelirian); hidup indiferen, penggunaannya tidak. Maka jangan lalai karenanya, tetapi juga jangan tunduk pada materi. Ingatlah pembagian milikku/bukan milikku — jangan mengklaim milik orang lain (misal: hasil pembicaraan dengan orang lain bukan tanggung jawabmu).","source_ids":["S289","S293"]},{"text":"Kematian itu kutukan bila dihindari: padi yang tidak pernah dipanen adalah kutukan; manusia yang tidak mati seperti tidak matang. Chrysantas menuruti terompet mundur daripada kehendaknya sendiri, sedangkan kita meratap menyebutnya 'keadaan' — padahal semua cara menuju Hades setara, bahkan jalan tiran lebih singkat daripada demam.","source_ids":["S290","S291"]},{"text":"Ramalan/divinasi sering dipakai karena pengecut — ketakutan pada masa depan — hingga melalaikan kewajiban (contoh: perempuan mengirim bantuan ke Gratilla yang diasingkan meski risiko disita Domitian). Konsultasi dengan Tuhan harus tanpa desire/aversion, seperti bertanya arah jalan kepada penumpang atau memakai mata; yang sejati adalah ramal internal dalam diri yang tanda baik-buruk.","source_ids":["S297","S298","S300"]},{"text":"Hakikat Baik: Tuhan bermanfaat, maka Baik ada di mana hakikat Tuhan ada — yaitu nalar benar dan kecerdasan dalam makhluk rasional, bukan pada tumbuhan atau hewan. Manusia adalah bagian terpisah dari dewa, 'membawa Tuhan di dalam dirinya' dan merusaknya dengan pikiran kotor; Tuhan menitipkan diri kita pada diri kita sendiri seperti titipan — jaganya agar sederhana, setia, bebas gejolak. Orang bijak mati dan sakit 'sebagaimana layaknya dewa'.","source_ids":["S303","S305","S307"]},{"text":"Kritik filsuf yang hanya bicara: menempatkan doktrin seperti roti di gudang, bukan yang telah dicerna menjadi daging dan tulang — hanya muncul bila kebisingan atau tawa mengganggu. Gagasan harus dipraktikkan setelah dipelajari; yang gagal memenuhi janji watak manusia (rasional) lalu menambahkan profesi filsuf seperti orang tak mampu mengangkat beban 10 pon mencoba mengangkat batu Ajax. Analogi: disebut Yahudi bukan dengan nama melainkan dengan pemilihan dan afek yang nyata.","source_ids":["S314","S316","S317"]},{"text":"Man adalah warga dunia yang rasional, yang tugasnya adalah bertindak sesuai dengan konstitusi alam dan tatanan ilahi (S321, S322). Karakter yang baik adalah tidak menganggap apa pun menguntungkan bagi diri sendiri dan bertindak sesuai peran (S321).","source_ids":["S321"]},{"text":"Kerusakan sejati bagi manusia bukanlah kehilangan harta atau tubuh, melainkan hilangnya karakter (seperti kesopanan atau ketenangan) yang merupakan bagian dari kehendak (will) (S324, S326).","source_ids":["S324","S326"]},{"text":"Filsafat dimulai dari kesadaran akan kelemahan diri dan ketidakmampuan untuk secara sempurna menyesuaikan prasangka bawaan (seperti baik/buruk) dengan kasus nyata. Tujuannya adalah menemukan aturan (kanonos) yang melampaui sekadar 'tampakan' atau 'perasaan' (S330, S333).","source_ids":["S330","S333"]},{"text":"Kecemasan (anxiety) muncul karena manusia menginginkan hal-hal yang berada di luar kekuasaannya (seperti pujian atau kehendak Caesar). Kepercayaan sejati hanya ada dalam penguasaan keadaan internal (keinginan dan keengganannya) (S347, S348).","source_ids":["S347","S348"]},{"text":"Tujuan praktis filsafat adalah menyesuaikan kehendak (will) dengan apa yang terjadi, sehingga seseorang dapat menjalani hidup tanpa ketakutan atau gangguan, baik dalam urusan pribadi maupun sosial (S358, S359).","source_ids":["S358","S359"]},{"text":"Langkah awal dalam filsafat adalah mempelajari providensi Tuhan dan berusaha meniru sifat-sifat ilahi (seperti kesetiaan dan kebebasan) dalam tindakan dan perkataan (S360).","source_ids":["S360"]},{"text":"Membedakan 'menggunakan' dan 'memahami': orang banyak memakai kata baik-buruk seperti buta huruf memakai tulisan atau hewan memakai penampakan. Seseorang yang kaya, punya keluarga dan teman Caesar, tetapi tak tahu apa itu Tuhan, manusia, baik dan jahat — bahkan tak tahu tentang dirinya sendiri. Kebenaran seperti cermin atau dokter: bukan penghinaan, meski orang mengeluh dihina bila dikatakan keinginannya menyala dan opiniannya gegabah.","source_ids":["S361","S362"]},{"text":"Mayoritas manusia seperti hewan di pasar: hanya sibuk dengan 'pakan' (harta, tanah, budak, jabatan). Sedikit yang datang untuk memperhatikan tatanan dunia — siapa yang mengaturnya, apa relasi kita dengan pengatur itu — dan karena itu ditertawakan banyak orang, seperti penonton ditertawakan pedagang di pasar.","source_ids":["S363","S364"]},{"text":"Kekerasan kepalaan pada keputusan bukanlah keteguhan: yang tetap dipegang hanyalah keputusan yang benar, seperti otot yang sehat, bukan kejang orang gila. Contoh teman yang memutuskan mati kelaparan tanpa alasan; jiwa sakit yang menambah keputusan gegabah jadi tak terbantu — 'orang bodoh tak bisa diyakinkan maupun dipecahkan'.","source_ids":["S367","S368","S370"]},{"text":"Baik ada di kemauan, jahat di kemauan, keduanya tidak ada di luar kemauan — tetapi kita tak pernah berlatih memberi jawaban benar di luar sekolah (ketika uang ditunjukkan: uang bukan baik). Rhetorician dan pemain lute gemetar di atas panggung karena tak dilatih tentang pujian dan cemoohan; ketakutan dan kecemasan bukan pekerjaan orang lain. Latihan sejati: takut pada ketakutan itu sendiri, bukan pada kematian atau pengasingan.","source_ids":["S373","S374","S377"]},{"text":"Yang memberatkan kita hanyalah opini: di laut lepas Epictetus sendiri terbayang harus meneguk seluruh laut, padahal tiga pint cukup. Kesedihan perpisahan seperti anak menangis ditinggal pengasuh — orang dewasa juga menangis untuk gimnasium, portikos, air Dirce, Akropolis; perlu 'disapih' ke makanan yang lebih padat. Hukum ilahi: jagakan milikmu, gunakan yang diberikan, serahkan kembali dengan senang hati.","source_ids":["S377","S379","S380","S383"]},{"text":"Membuang kembung diri (self-conceit) adalah tugas pertama filsuf: mustahil belajar apa yang sudah diyakini tahu. Preconception (prolepsis) tentang baik dan sehat sudah kita punya, tetapi tak bisa disesuaikan dengan kasus tanpa analisis dan definisi — sebab itu orang berdebat, seperti dokter terbelah sebelum Hippocrates. Bukti ketidakcocokan: keinginan yang tak terjadi. Medea punya opini benar bahwa keinginan gagal adalah sengsara, tapi salah tahu cara memenuhinya — jangan menginginkan yang di luar kuasa; serahkan desire/aversion kepada para dewa.","source_ids":["S389","S390","S392","S393","S394"]},{"text":"Melawan penampakan lewat kebiasaan: setiap tindakan memperkuat kebiasaannya — marah atau takabur menambah kebiasaan itu seperti menambah bahan bakar api; penyakit jiwa meninggalkan bekas (luka) yang bila tak dihapus total akan kambuh lebih parah. Obatnya: hitung hari tanpa marah, dan saat penampakan datang, tahan dulu — 'tunggu sedikit, biar aku lihat apa kamu' — lalu lawan dengan penampakan yang indah dan mulia. Kemenangan atas penampakan inilah atlet sejati, demi kerajaan, kebebasan, dan ketenangan.","source_ids":["S403","S404","S407","S409"]},{"text":"Kritik pada yang menerima filsafat hanya dalam kata-kata: mengetahui pembagian baik-buruk-indiferen dari Chrysippus atau Cleanthes tidak berbeda dari hafalan sejarah Homer; ujian sejati adalah apakah pembagian itu diingat saat badai di kapal atau saat dipanggil ke pengadilan Caesar. 'Tunjukkan aku seorang Stoik' — orang yang sakit, mati, diasingkan, dan tetap bahagia; bukan sekadar yang mengulang argumen kecil. Sekolah Epictetus bertujuan membuat murid bebas dan bahagia, dan satu-satunya yang dalam kuasa kita adalah penggunaan penampakan yang benar.","source_ids":["S420","S421","S422","S424"]},{"text":"Bantahan terhadap Epicurus dan Akademik: mereka yang menyangkal kebenaran justru memakainya — 'percayalah bahwa tak ada yang perlu dipercaya' adalah kontradiksi. Epicurus menyangkal persaudaraan alami manusia tetapi bangun tidur dan menulis buku untuk memperingatkan orang lain — sifat manusia yang tak terbantahkan memaksanya; seperti tanaman tak bisa tumbuh melawan jenisnya, manusia tak bisa menghapus afeksi kemanusiaan. Doktrin yang merusak kesalehan dan keadilan merusak negara, padahal Sparta dan Thermopylae dibangun dari opini yang sebaliknya.","source_ids":["S428","S429","S431","S434"]},{"text":"Ketidakkonsistenan orang dalam mengakui kesalahan: tak ada yang mengaku bodoh atau tidak adil, tetapi banyak yang mengaku penakut dan penyayang — karena kebingungan tentang baik-buruk; mereka menganggap ketakutan ciri watak baik dan tak mengakui kesalahan terhadap masyarakat.","source_ids":["S440"]},{"text":"Inkonsistensi moral: orang menganggap ketakutan, kasih sayang, cemburu, dan nafsu 'tidak disengaja' untuk membenarkan diri, tetapi ketidakadilan dianggap disengaja. Menghadapi murid yang datang ke sekolah hanya untuk menguasai syllogisme sambil bertengkar dengan budak di rumah; mereka membawa pulang persis yang mereka bawa—teorema tidak berguna bagi yang salah guna, seperti cuka tidak berguna bagi penderita disentri sebelum luka disembuhkan. Alasan mesti dibawa ke sekolah tenang dan bebas distraksi.","source_ids":["S441","S444","S445"]},{"text":"Persahabatan: hanya orang bijak yang mampu mencintai, karena cinta memerlukan pengetahuan tentang Baik. Setiap makhluk terikat pada kepentingannya sendiri; bila kepentingan diletakkan pada hal eksternal, saudara atau ayah pun bisa jadi musuh—seperti anjing yang bertengkar saat sepotong daging dilempar di antara mereka (Eteocles-Polynices, Alexander membakar kuil Aesculapius). Persahabatan sejati ada hanya bila kepentingan diletakkan pada will dan penggunaan penampakan yang benar.","source_ids":["S448","S454","S455"]},{"text":"Uji persahabatan: jangan percaya pada sumpah atau lahir dari orang tua sama—periksa di mana kepentingan orang itu diletakkan (hal luar atau will). 'Kamu menemani saya lama—tahu kamu tidak ia memperlakukanmu seperti membasuh sepatu dengan spons?'; kalung Eriphyle (opini tentang barang) merusak pernikahan Amphiaraus. Yang menempatkan diri pada will akan menjadi teman sejati dan memaafkan yang berbeda karena kebodohan (doktrin Plato: jiwa dirampas kebenaran dengan tak rela).","source_ids":["S456","S458","S459"]},{"text":"Kekuatan berbicara adalah hadiah Tuhan; menyangkalnya tidak syukur dan pengecut. Namun fakultas will adalah yang tertinggi: ia menggunakan semua fakultas lain sebagai pelayan, menilai nilai setiap fakultas, membuka-tutup mata dan telinga; hanya will sendiri yang bisa menghambat will—maka will itulah satu-satunya kebajikan atau kejahatan. Kritik Epicurus yang memposisikan daging sebagai yang terutama padahal daging tidak bisa menulis tentang tujuan hidup.","source_ids":["S462","S464","S466","S467"]},{"text":"Kekuatan bicara dan teorema hanyalah 'penginapan' di jalan pulang: jangan berhenti dan tinggal di sana seperti pelancong yang lupa tujuannya, terpikat pada ungkapan, syllogisme, atau sophisme seperti di antara Sirens. Tujuan sejati: menggunakan penampakan sesuai alam, desire tidak frustrasi, bebas, taat pada administrasi Zeus, tanpa menyalahkan siapa pun ('Lead me, O Zeus, and thou too Destiny'). Bicara seperti Demosthenes atau memecahkan syllogisme seperti Chrysippus tidak mencegah kecelakaan.","source_ids":["S472","S474","S476"]},{"text":"Ada juga seni mendengar: sebagaimana mendengar musik milik musisi dan menilai patung memerlukan seni, mendengar filsuf dengan bermanfaat memerlukan latihan khusus; tidak semua pendengar teruntung—yang mendengar terampil teruntung, yang tidak terampil merugi.","source_ids":["S479","S480"]},{"text":"Kesalahan (error) selalu mengandung kontradiksi: pencuri berpikir mencuri menguntungkan padahal tidak; jiwa rasional tak bisa menyetujui yang palsu bila kefalsahannya tampak. Maka sang pembaharu cukup menunjukkan kontradiksi itu—seperti Socrates yang cukup satu pembicara sebagai saksi—bila tak tampak, saling diri sendiri, bukan orangnya.","source_ids":["S492","S493"]},{"text":"Perawatan diri lewat penampilan (rambut berhias, mencabut bulu) dikritik: keindahan manusia ada pada keunggulan khasnya (keadilan, moderasi, kesederhanaan), bukan pada bagian hewani atau mortalitas; manusia adalah will (proairesis), bukan daging dan rambut. Socrates menasihati Alcibiades untuk menghiasi kemauan dan membuang opini buruk, bukan tubuh.","source_ids":["S496","S497","S508"]},{"text":"Filsuf wajib berkata benar meski pendengar tidak mau dipengaruhi: contoh Apollo tetap berbicara kepada Laius dan Socrates menolak berhenti mengajukan pertanyaan meski diadili; 'aku adalah orang yang bertugas merawat manusia'—yang unggul dalam setiap jenis (seperti ungu pada jubah, bulla melawan singa) tidak perlu membela diri atas keberbedaannya.","source_ids":["S500","S501","S502"]},{"text":"Tiga topik latihan orang yang berprogres: (1) desire/aversion—yang paling utama karena dari situ lahir gejolak; (2) tugas dan relasi alami (anak, ayah, warga) dengan afek yang tidak hampa seperti patung; (3) assent tanpa kekeliruan. Filsuf sezaman menelorkan topik ketiga (sophisme) sambil mengabaikan dua yang pertama—padahal bahkan terganggu oleh ketakutan diremehkan orang.","source_ids":["S512","S513","S514"]},{"text":"Nilai sejati tidak ditunjukkan dengan membaca Chrysippus/Archedemus: Diogenes menunjuk sophist dengan jari tengah—manusia ditunjukkan oleh prinsip-prinsipnya, bukan seperti batu. Yang kapalnya tenggelam tidak waktunya membahas argumen hipotetis; pembahasan logis hanya untuk yang sudah tenang, tanpa marah, duka, dan iri.","source_ids":["S515","S516","S517"]},{"text":"Materi kerja orang baik adalah fakultas penguasanya sendiri: menggunakan penampakan sesuai alam; jiwa tak bisa menolak penampakan baik yang jelas, seperti penukar uang tak bisa menolak koin Caesar—prinsip inilah dasar seluruh gerakan manusia dan Tuhan.","source_ids":["S520"]},{"text":"Baik lebih diutamakan daripada relasi terdekat: tidak ada relasi antara aku dan ayah, tetapi antara aku dan Baik. Bila Baik diletakkan pada penentuan kemauan yang benar, justru pemenuhan relasi hidup menjadi baik; ayah yang mengambil harta tidak melukai — kesopanan dan kesetiaan tak dapat dirampas bahkan oleh Zeus. Setiap orang punya 'koin' sendiri dari Tuhan (proconsul dibayar perak, pezina dengan gadis) yang menentukan apa yang ia beli.","source_ids":["S521","S522"]},{"text":"Latihan harian melawan penampakan: setiap pagi uji setiap penampakan dengan aturan — apakah dalam kuasa kemauan atau tidak; bila tidak, buang ('tidak ada bagimu'). Ratapan, sial, perpecahan sipil, celaan, kekufuran semuanya hanyalah opini tentang hal di luar kemauan seolah baik-buruk; pindahkan opini itu ke hal dalam kemauan maka orang akan teguh. Seperti cahaya di atas air yang bergoyang: jiwa yang terganggu tampak mengacaukan kebajikan, tetapi sebenarnya hanya roh yang perlu dikembalikan tenang.","source_ids":["S523","S524","S525"]},{"text":"Gubernur Epirus yang berseberangan di teater ditegur: banyak orang meniru contoh orang berkuasa; bila berseberangan itu salah, jangan lakukan sendiri; bila benar, jangan marah ditiru. Di teater masuklah dengan tujuan menjaga kemauan sesuai alam — 'tak ada yang lebih kusayang daripada diriku sendiri'; di rumah boleh menggelar permainan sendiri dan menobatkan Sophron, tetapi di publik jangan mengklaim milik semua orang; bila menolak, tanggunglah cemoohan.","source_ids":["S528","S529","S530"]},{"text":"Murid yang ingin pulang karena sakit ditegur: penyakit dan kematian pasti mengejutkan kita saat sedang melakukan sesuatu — berharap dikejutkan saat menjaga kemauan sendiri, agar bisa berkata kepada Tuhan: aku sakit dan miskin karena kehendak-Mu dan tetap pasrah, tak pernah mencela administrasi-Mu. Socrates bahagia karena tiap hari melihat dirinya bertumbuh lebih baik: tak pernah mencela siapa pun, Tuhan maupun manusia, dan selalu berwajah sama.","source_ids":["S533","S534","S537"]},{"text":"Orang baik tak terkalahkan karena tak masuk pertarungan di mana ia lebih lemah: tanah, budak, jabatan, tubuh boleh diambil, tetapi desire dan aversion-nya tak bisa digagalkan — satu-satunya pertarungan yang ia masuki adalah tentang hal dalam kuasa kemauannya. Kemajuan kini terhambat karena akal dilatih untuk memecahkan syllogisme, bukan untuk menjaga fakultas penguasa sesuai alam; jangan mencampur hal yang berbeda.","source_ids":["S540","S541"]},{"text":"Dialog dengan administrator Epicurean: jika daging yang terbaik, maka Maximus berlayar demi daging; tetapi kenikmatan jiwa harus bergantung pada sesuatu yang mendahuluinya — jika bukan hal jiwa, maka hal tubuh, dan substansi Baik jatuh ke tubuh. Konsekuensi logis Epicurean: mencuri dan berzina boleh bila tak terdeteksi — doktrin yang merusak negara dan keluarga. Tugas utama manusia: urusan publik, menikah, membesarkan anak, menghormati Tuhan, merawat orang tua; manusia terbawa bebas, mulia, dan mampu malu — kenikmatan harus jadi pelayan, bukan tuan.","source_ids":["S546","S549","S552","S553"]},{"text":"Kekuasaan menghukum bukan pemerintahan manusia: memenjarakan seperti batu, memukul seperti keledai. Pemerintahan sejati menunjukkan apa yang menguntungkan sebagai makhluk rasional, seperti Socrates. Hukuman bagi yang tak patuh bukan penjara, melainkan kehilangan watak: kesetiaan, kesopanan, kepatutan — jangan cari hukuman lebih besar dari itu.","source_ids":["S554","S555"]},{"text":"Latihan melawan penampakan seperti melawan soal sophistik: anakmu mati — apa yang terjadi? Anakmu mati, tidak lebih; 'ia sengsara' adalah tambahan opini sendiri. Bila menyalahkan Zeus, ingat: ia menjadimu mampu menanggung, menjadimu magnanimous, mengambil kuasa hal-hal menjadi kejahatan, dan membukakan pintu keluar — 'keluarlah dan jangan meratap'.","source_ids":["S558","S559"]},{"text":"Opini adalah sebab segala tindakan: Epictetus tak punya aturan apakah seseorang akan menang di Rome, hanya bahwa dengan opini benar ia berjalan baik. Filsuf yang ditemui hanya sekilas seperti batu bukan pertemuan sejati — bertukar dan menguji opini itulah maknanya. Yang kaya justru lebih miskin: butuh keteguhan, ketenangan, kebebasan dari kecemasan; keinginan yang banyak seperti tangan penuh buah dalam guci leher sempit — buang sebagian agar bisa keluar.","source_ids":["S563","S566","S567","S568"]},{"text":"Sakit adalah bagian hidup seperti berjalan dan berlayar; filosofi adalah persiapan menghadapi peristiwa — menyerah saat demam seperti mundur dari Pancratium setelah dipukul. Menanggung demam dengan baik: tak menyalahkan Tuhan atau manusia, menghadapi kematian dengan mulut, tak gentar atau gembira berlebihan pada kabar dokter. Dua prinsip siap sedia: selain will tak ada baik atau jahat, dan kita harus mengikuti peristiwa, bukan memimpinnya.","source_ids":["S573","S575","S576","S577"]},{"text":"Latihan (exercise) tidak boleh bertentangan dengan alam demi kekaguman (berjalan di tali, memeluk patung) — itu bedahara pesulap. Tujuannya: desire tak frustrasi dan aversion tak jatuh pada yang dihindari; lawan kebiasaan dengan kebiasaan sebaliknya. Pemula harus menjauhi yang lebih kuat darinya (gadis cantik vs pemula filosofi). Tiga topik latihan: desire/aversion, tindakan sesuai alasan, dan assent — periksa setiap penampakan seperti penjaga malam memeriksa izin.","source_ids":["S586","S587","S589","S590"]},{"text":"Kesendirian (solitude) adalah kondisi tak berdaya, bukan sekadar sendiri — bahkan Zeus sendiri di konflagrasi tak menyendiri. Manusia harus mampu jadi teman dirinya sendiri seperti Zeus: memperhatikan administrasi ilahi dan relasi dirinya dengan segala hal. Damai dari Caesar tak melindungi dari demam, kapal karam, cinta, duka; doktrin filosof menjanjikan ketenangan dari semuanya — dan kematian adalah pintu pulang ke unsur-unsur, penuh dewa, bukan Hades.","source_ids":["S594","S595","S596","S597"]},{"text":"Kekuatan besar berbahaya bagi pemula: berlatih menahan diri (makan sedikit, air, menahan desire) agar kelak menginginkan sesuai alasan; berbuat baik lewat contoh hidup, bukan ceramah. Penalti ilahi bagi yang menempatkan baik di luar will: ia akan iri, menyanjung, gelisah; yang menempatkan jahat di luar will akan berduka dan menangis. Setiap relasi (ayah, saudara) diawasi Zeus.","source_ids":["S580","S583","S599"]}],"sources":[{"id":"S641","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists"},{"id":"S642","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"They who have taken up bare theorems (θεωρήματα) immediately wish to vomit them forth, as persons whose stomach is diseased do with food. First digest the thing, then do not vomit it up thus; if you do not digest it, the thing becomes truly an emetic, a crude food and unfit to eat. But after digestion show us some change in your ruling faculty, as athletes show in their shoulders by what they have been exercised and what they have eaten; as those who have taken up certain arts show by what they have learned. The carpenter does not come and say, “Hear me talk about the carpenter’s art,” but having undertaken to build a house, he makes it, and proves that he knows the art. You also ought to do something of the kind: eat like a man, drink like a man, dress, marry, beget children, do the office of a citizen, endure abuse, bear with an unreasonable brother, bear with your father, bear with your son, neighbour, companion. Show us these things that we may see that you have in truth learned something from the philosophers. You say, “No; but come and hear me read (philosophical) commentaries.” Go away, and seek somebody to vomit them on. (He replies) “And indeed I will expound to you the wr"},{"id":"S643","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"itings of Chrysippus as no other man can: I will explain his text most clearly: I will add also, if I can, the vehemence of Antipater and Archedemus.”"},{"id":"S644","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"Is it then for this that young men shall leave their country and their parents, that they may come to this place, and hear you explain words? Ought they not to return with a capacity to endure, to be active in association with others, free from passions, free from perturbation, with such a provision for the journey of life with which they shall be able to bear well the things that happen and derive honor from them? And how can you give them any of these things which you do not possess? Have you done from the beginning anything else than employ yourself about the resolution of Syllogisms, of sophistical arguments (οἱ μεταπίπτοντες), and in those which work by questions? “But such a man has a school; why should not I also have a school?” These things are not done, man, in a careless way, nor just as it may happen; but there must be a (fit) age and life and God as a guide. You say, “No.” But no man sails from a port without having sacrificed to the Gods and invoked their help; nor do men sow without having called on Demeter; and shall a man who has undertaken so great a work undertake it safely without the Gods? and shall they who undertake this work come to it with success? What else"},{"id":"S645","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":" are you doing, man, than divulging the mysteries? You say, “there is a temple at Eleusis, and one here also. There is an Hierophant at Eleusis, and I also will make an Hierophant: there is a herald, and I will establish a herald: there is a torchbearer at Eleusis, and I also will establish a torchbearer; there are torches at Eleusis, and I will have torches here. The words are the same: how do the things done here differ from those done there?” Most impious man, is there no difference? these things are done both in due place and in due time; and when accompanied with sacrifice and prayers, when a man is first purified, and when he is disposed in his mind to the thought that he is going to approach sacred rites and ancient rites. In this way the mysteries are useful, in this way we come to the notion that all these things were established by the ancients for the instruction and correction of life. But you publish and divulge them out of time, out of place, without sacrifices, without purity; you have not the garments which the hierophant ought to have, nor the hair, nor the headdress, nor the voice, nor the age; nor have you purified yourself as he has: but you have committed to me"},{"id":"S646","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"mory the words only, and you say, “Sacred are the words by themselves.” You ought to approach these matters in another way: the thing is great, it is mystical, not a common thing, nor is it given to every man. But not even wisdom perhaps is enough to enable a man to take care of youths: a man must have also a certain readiness and fitness for this purpose, and a certain quality of body, and above all things he must have God to advise him to occupy this office, as God advised Socrates to occupy the place of one who confutes error, Diogenes the office of royalty and reproof, and the office of teaching precepts. But you open a doctor’s shop, though you have nothing except physic: but where and how they should be applied, you know not nor have you taken any trouble about it. “See,” that man says, “I too have salves for the eyes.” Have you also the power of using them? Do you know both when and how they will do good, and to whom they will do good? Why then do you act at hazard in things of the greatest importance? why are you careless? why do you undertake a thing that is in no way fit for you? Leave it to those who are able to do it, and to do it well. Do not yourself bring disgrace on"},{"id":"S647","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":" philosophy through your own acts, and be not one of those who load it with a bad reputation. But if theorems please you, sit still, and turn them over by yourself; but never say that you are a philosopher, nor allow another to say it; but say: “He is mistaken, for neither are my desires different from what they were before, nor is my activity directed to other objects, nor do I assent to other things, nor in the use of appearances have I altered at all from my former condition.” This you must think and say about yourself, if you would think as you ought: if not act at hazard, and do what you are doing; for it becomes you."},{"id":"S648","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XXII"},{"id":"S649","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"About Cynism"},{"id":"S650","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"When one of his pupils inquired of Epictetus, and he was a person who appeared to be inclined to Cynism, what kind of person a Cynic ought to be and what was the notion (πρόληψις) of the thing —we will inquire, said Epictetus, at leisure: but I have so much to say to you that he who without God attempts so great a matter, is hateful to God, and has no other purpose than to act indecently in public. For in any well-managed house no man comes forward, and says to himself, I ought to be manager of the house. If he does so, the master turns round, and seeing him insolently giving orders, drags him forth and flogs him. So it is also in this great city (the world); for here also there is a master of the house who orders everything. (He says) “You are the sun; you can by going round make the year and seasons, and make the fruits grow and nourish them, and stir the winds and make them remit, and warm the bodies of men properly: go, travel round, and so administer things from the greatest to the least. You are a calf; when a lion shall appear, do your proper business (i.e. run away): if you do not, you will suffer. You are a bull: advance and fight, for this is your business, and becomes yo"},{"id":"S651","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"u, and you can do it. You can lead the army against Ilium; be Agamemnon. You can fight in single combat against Hector: be Achilles.” But if Thersites came forward and claimed the command, he would either not have obtained it; or if he did obtain it, he would have disgraced himself before many witnesses."},{"id":"S652","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"Do you also think about the matter carefully: it is not what it seems to you. (You say) “I wear a cloak now and I shall wear it then; I sleep hard now, and I shall sleep hard then; I will take in addition a little bag now and a staff, and I will go about and begin to beg and to abuse those whom I meet; and if I see any man plucking the hair out of his body, I will rebuke him, or if he has dressed his hair, or if he walks about in purple.” If you imagine the thing to be such as this, keep far away from it; do not approach it; it is not at all for you. But if you imagine it to be what it is, and do not think yourself to be unfit for it, consider what a great thing you undertake."},{"id":"S653","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":4,"paragraphEnd":4,"text":"In the first place, in the things which relate to yourself, you must not be in any respect like what you do now: you must not blame God or man; you must take away desire altogether, you must transfer avoidance (ἔκκλισις) only to the things which are within the power of the will; you must not feel anger nor resentment nor envy nor pity; a girl must not appear handsome to you, nor must you love a little reputation, nor be pleased with a boy or a cake. For you ought to know that the rest of men throw walls around them and houses and darkness when they do any such things, and they have many means of concealment. A man shuts the door, he sets somebody before the chamber: “if a person comes, say that he is out, he is not at leisure.” But the Cynic instead of all these things must use modesty as his protection: if he does not, he will be indecent in his nakedness and under the open sky. This is his house, his door; this is the slave before his bedchamber; this is his darkness. For he ought not to wish to hide anything that he does; and if he does, he is gone: he has lost the character of a Cynic, of a man who lives under the open sky, of a free man; he has begun to fear some external thin"},{"id":"S654","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":4,"paragraphEnd":4,"text":"g, he has begun to have need of concealment, nor can he get concealment when he chooses. For where shall he hide himself and how? And if by chance this public instructor shall be detected, this pedagogue, what kind of things will he be compelled to suffer? When then a man fears these things, is it possible for him to be bold with his whole soul to superintend men? It cannot be: it is impossible."},{"id":"S655","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":5,"paragraphEnd":5,"text":"In the first place then you must make your ruling faculty pure, and this mode of life also. “Now” (you should say), “to me the matter to work on is my understanding, as wood is to the carpenter, as hides to the shoemaker; and my business is the right use of appearances. But the body is nothing to me; the parts of it are nothing to me. Death? Let it come when it chooses, either death of the whole or of a part. Fly, you say. And whither; can any man eject me out of the world? He cannot. But wherever I go, there is the sun, there is the moon, there are the stars, dreams, omens, and the conversation (ὁμιλία) with Gods.”"},{"id":"S656","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":6,"paragraphEnd":6,"text":"Then, if he is thus prepared, the true Cynic cannot be satisfied with this, but he must know that he is sent a messenger from Zeus to men about good and bad things, to show them that they have wandered and are seeking the substance of good and evil where it is not, but where it is, they never think; and that he is a spy, as Diogenes was carried off to Philip after the battle of Chaeroneia as a spy. For in fact a Cynic is a spy of the things which are good for men and which are evil, and it is his duty to examine carefully and to come and report truly, and not to be struck with terror so as to point out as enemies those who are not enemies, nor in any other way to be perturbed by appearances nor confounded."},{"id":"S657","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":7,"paragraphEnd":7,"text":"It is his duty then to be able with a loud voice, if the occasion should arise, and appearing on the tragic stage, to say like Socrates: Men, whither are you hurrying, what are you doing, wretches? like blind people you are wandering up and down: you are going by another road, and have left the true road: you seek for prosperity and happiness where they are not, and if another shows you where they are, you do not believe him. Why do you seek it without? In the body? It is not there. If you doubt, look at Myro, look at Ophellius. In possessions? It is not there. But if you do not believe me, look at Croesus: look at those who are now rich, with what lamentations their life is filled. In power? It is not there. If it is, those must be happy who have been twice and thrice consuls; but they are not. Whom shall we believe in these matters? You who from without see their affairs and are dazzled by an appearance, or the men themselves? What do they say? Hear them when they groan, when they grieve, when on account of these very consulships and glory and splendour they think that they are more wretched and in greater danger. Is it in royal power? It is not: if it were, Nero would have been "},{"id":"S658","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":7,"paragraphEnd":7,"text":"happy, and Sardanapalus. But neither was Agamemnon happy, though he was a better man than Sardanapalus and Nero; but while others are snoring, what is he doing?"},{"id":"S659","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":8,"paragraphEnd":8,"text":"Much from his head he tore his rooted hair:"},{"id":"S660","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":9,"paragraphEnd":9,"text":"— Iliad, x 15"},{"id":"S661","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":10,"paragraphEnd":10,"text":"and what does he say himself?"},{"id":"S662","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":11,"paragraphEnd":11,"text":"“I am perplexed,” he says, “and\nDisturb’d I am,” and “my heart out of my bosom\nIs leaping.”"},{"id":"S663","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":12,"paragraphEnd":12,"text":"— Iliad x 91"},{"id":"S664","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":13,"paragraphEnd":13,"text":"Wretch, which of your affairs goes badly? Your possessions? No. Your body? No. But you are rich in gold and copper. What then is the matter with you? That part of you, whatever it is, has been neglected by you and is corrupted, the part with which we desire, with which we avoid, with which we move towards and move from things. How neglected? He knows not the nature of good for which he is made by nature, and the nature of evil; and what is his own, and what belongs to another; and when anything that belongs to others goes badly, he says, “Woe to me, for the Hellenes are in danger.” Wretched is his ruling faculty, and alone neglected and uncared for. “The Hellenes are going to die destroyed by the Trojans.” And if the Trojans do not kill them, will they not die? “Yes; but not all at once.” What difference then does it make? For if death is an evil, whether men die altogether, or if they die singly, it is equally an evil. Is anything else then going to happen than the separation of the soul and the body? Nothing. And if the Hellenes perish, is the door closed, and is it not in your power to die? It is. Why then do you lament (and say) “Oh, you who are a king and have the sceptre of Z"},{"id":"S665","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":13,"paragraphEnd":13,"text":"eus?” An unhappy king does not exist more than an unhappy god. What then art thou? In truth a shepherd: for you weep as shepherds do, when a wolf has carried off one of their sheep: and these who are governed by you are sheep. And why did you come hither? Was your desire in any danger? was your aversion (ἔκκλισις)? was your movement (pursuits)? was your avoidance of things? He replies, “No; but the wife of my brother was carried off.” Was it not then a great gain to be deprived of an adulterous wife? “Shall we be despised then by the Trojans?” What kind of people are the Trojans, wise or foolish? If they are wise, why do you fight with them? If they are fools, why do you care about them?"},{"id":"S666","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":14,"paragraphEnd":14,"text":"In what then is the good, since it is not in these things? Tell us, you who are lord, messenger, and spy. Where you do not think that it is, nor choose to seek it: for if you chose to seek it, you would have found it to be in yourselves; nor would you be wandering out of the way, nor seeking what belongs to others as if it were your own. Turn your thoughts into yourselves: observe the preconceptions which you have. What kind of a thing do you imagine the good to be? “That which flows easily, that which is happy, that which is not impeded.” Come, and do you not naturally imagine it to be great, do you not imagine it to be valuable? do you not imagine it to be free from harm? In what material then ought you to seek for that which flows easily, for that which is not impeded? in that which serves or in that which is free? “In that which is free.” Do you possess the body then free or is it in servile condition? “We do not know.” Do you not know that it is the slave of fever, of gout, ophthalmia, dysentery, of a tyrant, of fire, of iron, of everything which is stronger? “Yes, it is a slave.” How then is it possible that anything which belongs to the body can be free from hindrance? and h"},{"id":"S667","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":14,"paragraphEnd":14,"text":"ow is a thing great or valuable which is naturally dead, or earth, or mud? Well then, do you possess nothing which is free? “Perhaps nothing.” And who is able to compel you to assent to that which appears false? “No man.” And who can compel you not to assent to that which appears true? “No man.” By this then you see that there is something in you naturally free. But to desire or to be averse from, or to move towards an object or to move from it, or to prepare yourself, or to propose to do anything, which of you can do this, unless he has received an impression of the appearance of that which is profitable or a duty? “No man.” You have then in these things also something which is not hindered and is free. Wretched men, work out this, take care of this, seek for good here."},{"id":"S668","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":15,"paragraphEnd":15,"text":"“And how is it possible that a man who has nothing, who is naked, houseless, without a hearth, squalid, without a slave, without a city, can pass a life that flows easily?” See, God has sent you a man to show you that it is possible. Look at me, who am without a city, without a house, without possessions, without a slave; I sleep on the ground; I have no wife, no children, no praetorium, but only the earth and heavens, and one poor cloak. And what do I want? Am I not without sorrow? am I not without fear? Am I not free? When did any of you see me failing in the object of my desire? or ever falling into that which I would avoid? did I ever blame God or man? did I ever accuse any man? did any of you ever see me with sorrowful countenance? And how do I meet with those whom you are afraid of and admire? Do not I treat them like slaves? Who, when he sees me, does not think that he sees his king and master?"},{"id":"S669","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":16,"paragraphEnd":16,"text":"This is the language of the Cynics, this their character, this is their purpose. You say “No: but their characteristic is the little wallet, and staff, and great jaws: the devouring of all that you give them, or storing it up, or the abusing unseasonably all whom they meet, or displaying their shoulder as a fine thing.” Do you see how you are going to undertake so great a business? First take a mirror: look at your shoulders; observe your loins, your thighs. You are going, my man, to be enrolled as a combatant in the Olympic games, no frigid and miserable contest. In the Olympic games a man is not permitted to be conquered only and to take his departure; but first he must be disgraced in the sight of all the world, not in the sight of Athenians only, or of Lacedaemonians, or of Nicopolitans; next he must be whipped also if he has entered into the contests rashly: and before being whipped, he must suffer thirst and heat, and swallow much dust."},{"id":"S670","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":17,"paragraphEnd":17,"text":"Reflect more carefully, know thyself, consult the divinity, without God attempt nothing; for if he shall advise you (to do this or anything), be assured that he intends you to become great or to receive many blows. For this very amusing quality is conjoined to a Cynic: he must be flogged like an ass, and when he is flogged, he must love those who flog him, as if he were the father of all, and the brother of all. —You say “No; but if a man flogs you, stand in the public place and call out, ‘Caesar, what do I suffer in this state of peace under thy protection?’ Let us bring the offender before the proconsul.” But what is Caesar to a Cynic, or what is a proconsul or what is any other except him who sent the Cynic down hither, and whom he serves, namely Zeus? Does he call upon any other than Zeus? Is he not convinced that whatever he suffers, it is Zeus who is exercising him? Hercules when he was exercised by Eurystheus did not think that he was wretched, but without hesitation he attempted to execute all that he had in hand. And is he who is trained to the contest and exercised by Zeus going to call out and to be vexed, he who is worthy to bear the sceptre of Diogenes? Hear what Dioge"},{"id":"S671","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":17,"paragraphEnd":17,"text":"nes says to the passers by when he is in a fever, “Miserable wretches, will you not stay? but are you going so long a journey to Olympia to see the destruction or the fight of athletes; and will you not choose to see the combat between a fever and a man?” Would such a man accuse God who sent him down as if God were treating him unworthily, a man who gloried in his circumstances, and claimed to be an example to those who were passing by? For what shall he accuse him of? because he maintains a decency of behavior, because he displays his virtue more conspicuously? Well, and what does he say of poverty, about death, about pain? How did he compare his own happiness with that of the great king (the king of Persia)? or rather he thought that there was no comparison between them. For where there are perturbations, and griefs, and fears, and desires not satisfied, and aversions of things which you cannot avoid, and envies, and jealousies, how is there a road to happiness there? But where there are corrupt principles, there these things must of necessity be."},{"id":"S672","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":18,"paragraphEnd":18,"text":"When the young man asked, if “when a Cynic has fallen sick, and a friend asks him to come to his house and to be taken care of in his sickness, shall the Cynic accept the invitation,” he replied: And where shall you find, I ask, a Cynic’s friend? For the man who invites ought to be such another as the Cynic that he may be worthy of being reckoned the Cynic’s friend. He ought to be a partner in the Cynic’s sceptre and his royalty, and a worthy minister, if he intends to be considered worthy of a Cynic’s friendship, as Diogenes was a friend of Antisthenes, as Crates was a friend of Diogenes. Do you think that if a man comes to a Cynic and salutes him, that he is the Cynic’s friend, and that the Cynic will think him worthy of receiving a Cynic into his house? So that if you please, reflect on this also: rather look round for some convenient dunghill on which you shall bear your fever and which will shelter you from the north wind that you may not be chilled. But you seem to me to wish to go into some man’s house and to be well fed there for a time. Why then do you think of attempting so great a thing (as the life of a Cynic)?"},{"id":"S673","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":19,"paragraphEnd":19,"text":"“But,” said the young man, “shall marriage and the procreation of children as a chief duty be undertaken by the Cynic?” If you grant me a community of wise men, Epictetus replies, perhaps no man will readily apply himself to the Cynic practice. For on whose account should he undertake this manner of life? However if we suppose that he does, nothing will prevent him from marrying and begetting children; for his wife will be another like himself, and his father in law another like himself, and his children will be brought up like himself. But in the present state of things which is like that of an army placed in battle order, is it not fit that the Cynic should without any distraction be employed only on the ministration of God, able to go about among men, not tied down to the common duties of mankind, nor entangled in the ordinary relations of life, which if he neglects, he will not maintain the character of an honorable and good man? and if he observes them he will lose the character of the messenger, and spy, and herald of God. For consider that it is his duty to do something towards his father in law, something to the other kinsfolks of his wife, something to his wife also (if he"},{"id":"S674","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":19,"paragraphEnd":19,"text":" has one). He is also excluded by being a Cynic from looking after the sickness of his own family, and from providing for their support. And to say nothing of the rest, he must have a vessel for heating water for the child that he may wash it in the bath; wool for his wife when she is delivered of a child, oil, a bed, a cup: so the furniture of the house is increased. I say nothing of his other occupations, and of his distraction. Where then now is that king, he who devotes himself to the public interests,"},{"id":"S675","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":20,"paragraphEnd":20,"text":"The people’s guardian and so full of cares."},{"id":"S676","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":21,"paragraphEnd":21,"text":"— Homer, Iliad ii 25"},{"id":"S677","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":22,"paragraphEnd":22,"text":"whose duty it is to look after others, the married and those who have children; to see who uses his wife well, who uses her badly; who quarrels; what family is well administered, what is not; going about as a physician does and feels pulses? He says to one, you have a fever, to another you have a headache, or the gout; he says to one, abstain from food; to another he says, eat; or do not use the bath; to another, you require the knife, or the cautery. How can he have time for this who is tied to the duties of common life? Is it not his duty to supply clothing to his children, and to send them to the schoolmaster with writing tablets and styles (for writing). Besides must he not supply them with beds? for they cannot be genuine Cynics as soon as they are born. If he does not do this, it would be better to expose the children as soon as they are born than to kill them in this way. Consider what we are bringing the Cynic down to, how we are taking his royalty from him. “Yes, but Crates took a wife.” You are speaking of a circumstance which arose from love and of a woman who was another Crates. But we are inquiring about ordinary marriages and those which are free from distractions, an"},{"id":"S678","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":22,"paragraphEnd":22,"text":"d making this inquiry we do not find the affair of marriage in this state of the world a thing which is especially suited to the Cynic."},{"id":"S679","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":23,"paragraphEnd":23,"text":"How then shall a man maintain the existence of society? In the name of God, are those men greater benefactors to society who introduce into the world to occupy their own places two or three grunting children, or those who superintend as far as they can all mankind, and see what they do, how they live, what they attend to, what they neglect contrary to their duty? Did they who left little children to the Thebans do them more good than Epaminondas who died childless? And did Priamus who begat fifty worthless sons or Danaus or Aeolus contribute more to the community than Homer? Then shall the duty of a general or the business of a writer exclude a man from marriage or the begetting of children, and such a man shall not be judged to have accepted the condition of childlessness for nothing; and shall not the royalty of a Cynic be considered an equivalent for the want of children? Do we not perceive his grandeur and do we not justly contemplate the character of Diogenes; and do we instead of this turn our eyes to the present Cynics who are dogs that wait at tables, and in no respect imitate the Cynics of old except perchance in breaking wind, but in nothing else? For such matters would n"},{"id":"S680","chapter":"XXII: About Cynism","paragraphStart":23,"paragraphEnd":23,"text":"ot have moved us at all nor should we have wondered if a Cynic should not marry or beget children. Man, the Cynic is the father of all men; the men are his sons, the women are his daughters: he so carefully visits all, so well does he care for all. Do you think that it is from idle impertinence that he rebukes those whom he meets? He does it as a father, as a brother, and as the minister of the father of all, the minister of Zeus."}],"newWindowIds":["S641","S642","S643","S644","S645","S646","S647","S648","S649","S650","S651","S652","S653","S654","S655","S656","S657","S658","S659","S660","S661","S662","S663","S664","S665","S666","S667","S668","S669","S670","S671","S672","S673","S674","S675","S676","S677","S678","S679","S680"]}

Contoh: Lateranus mengulurkan leher dengan tenang; Agrippinus tetap makan setelah dijatuhi hukuman pengasingan.","source_ids":["S9","S11","S12"]},{"text":"Menjaga karakter (proper character): yang rasional selalu diterima, yang irasional tak tertanggungkan — karena itu kita butuh disiplin. Alam berakhir pada kontemplasi dan hidup sesuai alam; memulai dan berakhir seperti hewan adalah memalukan.","source_ids":["S48","S49"]},{"text":"Providence: dari segala yang ada dan terjadi mudah memuji providensi bila memiliki dua hal — kemampuan melihat kegunaan segala hal dan watak bersyukur. Kebebasan adalah belajar menginginkan segala sesuatu terjadi sebagaimana terjadi; yang tidak menerima hukumannya adalah menjadi dirinya sendiri—di mana ia berada dengan tidak rela, di situ ia dipenjara (Socrates tidak dipenjara karena ada dengan rela).","source_ids":["S103","S104","S107"]},{"text":"Tuhan mengawasi segala hal: jiwa kita adalah bagian dan potongan dari Tuhan, dan setiap manusia diberi penjaga (daimon) yang tidak pernah tidur; kita harus bersumpah kepada Tuhan—tidak pernah membangkang, tidak mencela apa yang diberikan, dan tidak dengan enggan melakukan atau menderita apa yang perlu—sumpah yang menghormati diri sendiri, bukan Caesar.","source_ids":["S115","S117","S118"]},{"text":"Filosofi tidak menjanjikan hal eksternal apa pun; materinya adalah hidup orang itu sendiri. Kebenaran besar tidak terbentuk tiba-tiba, seperti buah ara butuh waktu matang.","source_ids":["S121","S123"]},{"text":"Providence terlihat bahkan dalam hal kecil: susu dari rumput, keju dari susu, rambut dagu sebagai tanda pembeda pria-wanita.
