Kehancuran sejati adalah kehancuran opini benar: Alexander hancur saat kehilangan karakter, Achilles saat marah dan lupa tugasnya.","source_ids":["S214","S216","S217"]},{"text":"Esensi Baik adalah kemauan; hal luar hanya bahan bagi kemauan. Hukum Allah: ambil kebaikan dari dirimu sendiri. Tirani hanya mengancam tubuh; tidak ada yang lebih kuat daripada kemauan kecuali kemauan sendiri—sepuluh orang lebih kuat dalam mengekang, tetapi tidak dalam opini yang benar.","source_ids":["S222","S224"]},{"text":"Socrates menafsir ulang: yang dibawa ke penjara hanyalah 'tubuh miskinnya'; 'Anytus dan Melitus dapat membunuhku, tetapi tidak menyakitiku.' Kesulitan adalah ujian pembelajaran: seperti atlet yang ingin lawan berat, orang terdidik harus menunjukkan ajarannya dalam praktik, bukan argumen kecil di sudut sekolah; jadilah saksi Allah bahwa yang eksternal bukan baik atau jahat.","source_ids":["S226","S232","S235"]},{"text":"Pelayan yang baik menghormati semua orang sesuai 'relasi': ayah, saudara, keabadian—mengingat bahwa adalah watak dewata mempertahankan diri dari mimpi dan kecenderungan; putusan orang yang belum terdidik tentang kesalehan tidak lebih penting daripada seorang musisi yang salah menilai tali lyre. Hamba yang lari menikmati teater dengan ketakutan; membebaskan diri dari 'majikan' (kematian, kesenangan, sakit) menghapus seluruh ketakutan.","source_ids":["S236","S238","S239"]},{"text":"Sikap yang harus disiapkan dalam kesulitan: saat menghadapi orang besar, ingat ada yang melihat dari atas; pengasingan, penjara, mati, aib tetap hal indiferen yang tak berubah — hanya hal di luar kemauan yang 'tak ada bagiku'; Baik adalah kemauan sebagaimana mestinya dan penggunaan penampakan; tujuan hidup adalah mengikuti Tuhan. YAng begitu belajar akan berani karena tahu semua persiapan gelar-gelar kuasa 'bukanlah apa-apa'.","source_ids":["S243","S244"]},{"text":"Percaya diri dan kehati-hatian tidak bertentangan bila diterapkan pada objek berbeda: kehati-hatian pada hal dalam kemauan (satu-satunya jahat), keberanian pada hal di luar kemauan. Manusia terbalik seperti rusa yang takut pada bulu pemburu lalu lari ke jaring: takut pada kematian, sakit, aib (hal luar) tetapi gegabah pada tipu, nafsu, aib tindakan (hal will). Bukan kematian yang menakutkan, melainkan ketakutan pada kematian.","source_ids":["S247","S248","S249"]},{"text":"Kematian dan sakit adalah 'topeng tragedi': putar dan periksa — tidak menggigit; pintu selalu terbuka bila tak tertahankan. Kebebasan sejati adalah milik yang terdidik: hidup tanpa kesalahan, takut, duka, dan gejolak adalah bebas; budak yang dibebaskan di pengadilan tetap tak bebas bila uang, kekasih, atau tiran jadi majikannya. Socrates menulis untuk menguji dirinya sendiri dalam praktik, bukan karya-karya kosong; pamer sejati pemuda terdidik adalah 'sajikan kematian, penjara, siksaan — aku tak kecewa dan tak jatuh'.","source_ids":["S252","S254","S257","S258"]},{"text":"Ketenangan dalam perkara (contoh: ke pengadilan): bila tujuannya mempertahankan will sesuai alam, aman penuh — tak ada yang menguasainya; bila ingin mempertahankan hal luar, siaplah jadi budak penuh (berlutut, menangis). Socrates seumur hidup bersiap menghadapi sidang karena tak pernah berbuat zalim. Minta 'saran untuk setiap kejadian' seperti orang buta huruf minta tahu nama apa yang akan ditulis; latihan membuat siap untuk semua, dan yang mengejar hal luar pasti terombang-ambing pada kehendak majikannya.","source_ids":["S262","S263","S264","S267"]},{"text":"Magnanimitas konsisten dengan kehati-hatian lewat analogi meja judi: keping dan dadanya indiferen, tetapi penggunaan lemparan harus cermat — hal luar tak milik kita, will milik kita; gunakan hal luar dengan hati-hati karena penggunaannya bukan indiferen, sambil tetap tenang karena materinya indiferen. Seperti pelayaran: pilih kapten, pelaut, waktu; datang badai, tugas kita selesai — bila kapal tenggelam, lakukan satu-satunya yang bisa: tidak tenggelam.","source_ids":["S279","S280"]},{"text":"Manusia dibentuk untuk kesetiaan (fidelity); perusaknya meruntuhkan ciri khas manusia: kesopanan, kesucian, hubungan tetangga, persahabatan, komunitas — jadilah serigala atau kera, dan layak dibuang seperti peralatan rusak ke tumpukan kotoran. Argumen 'wanita memang bersifat umum secara alam' dibantah dengan analogi: babi dan teater juga umum bagi semua, tetapi setelah dibagikan, mencuri porsi orang lain adalah perampokan.","source_ids":["S274","S276"]},{"text":"Metafora permainan bola: keahlian ada pada melempar dan menangkap, bukan pada bola itu sendiri — bola (hal eksternal) harus dianggap tak berharga. Socrates bermain bola di pengadilannya: omongannya yang menyenangkan pada Anytus adalah lemparan; bolanya adalah hidup, belenggu, racun. Kita harus mengerahkan seluruh keahlian pada materi eksternal tanpa menghargai materinya, seperti tukang tenun yang mengerjakan wol apa pun yang diterimanya.","source_ids":["S282","S283"]},{"text":"Foot analogy: manusia adalah bagian dari keseluruhan, bukan makhluk terpisah — kaki yang menjejak lumpur atau dipotong demi tubuh masih sesuai alam sebagai kaki; manusia yang sakit, miskin, atau mati muda tetap sesuai alam sebagai bagian dari negara yang pertama (dewa dan manusia). Hidup seperti satu jam dalam sehari: hadir lalu lewat; bagaimana cara berlalunya tak penting.","source_ids":["S281","S285"]},{"text":"Hal indiferen vs penilaiannya: proposisi hipotetis indiferen, tetapi penilaian tentangnya tidak (pengetahuan, opini, atau kekelirian); hidup indiferen, penggunaannya tidak. Maka jangan lalai karenanya, tetapi juga jangan tunduk pada materi. Ingatlah pembagian milikku/bukan milikku — jangan mengklaim milik orang lain (misal: hasil pembicaraan dengan orang lain bukan tanggung jawabmu).","source_ids":["S289","S293"]},{"text":"Kematian itu kutukan bila dihindari: padi yang tidak pernah dipanen adalah kutukan; manusia yang tidak mati seperti tidak matang. Chrysantas menuruti terompet mundur daripada kehendaknya sendiri, sedangkan kita meratap menyebutnya 'keadaan' — padahal semua cara menuju Hades setara, bahkan jalan tiran lebih singkat daripada demam.","source_ids":["S290","S291"]},{"text":"Ramalan/divinasi sering dipakai karena pengecut — ketakutan pada masa depan — hingga melalaikan kewajiban (contoh: perempuan mengirim bantuan ke Gratilla yang diasingkan meski risiko disita Domitian). Konsultasi dengan Tuhan harus tanpa desire/aversion, seperti bertanya arah jalan kepada penumpang atau memakai mata; yang sejati adalah ramal internal dalam diri yang tanda baik-buruk.","source_ids":["S297","S298","S300"]},{"text":"Hakikat Baik: Tuhan bermanfaat, maka Baik ada di mana hakikat Tuhan ada — yaitu nalar benar dan kecerdasan dalam makhluk rasional, bukan pada tumbuhan atau hewan. Manusia adalah bagian terpisah dari dewa, 'membawa Tuhan di dalam dirinya' dan merusaknya dengan pikiran kotor; Tuhan menitipkan diri kita pada diri kita sendiri seperti titipan — jaganya agar sederhana, setia, bebas gejolak. Orang bijak mati dan sakit 'sebagaimana layaknya dewa'.","source_ids":["S303","S305","S307"]},{"text":"Kritik filsuf yang hanya bicara: menempatkan doktrin seperti roti di gudang, bukan yang telah dicerna menjadi daging dan tulang — hanya muncul bila kebisingan atau tawa mengganggu. Gagasan harus dipraktikkan setelah dipelajari; yang gagal memenuhi janji watak manusia (rasional) lalu menambahkan profesi filsuf seperti orang tak mampu mengangkat beban 10 pon mencoba mengangkat batu Ajax. Analogi: disebut Yahudi bukan dengan nama melainkan dengan pemilihan dan afek yang nyata.","source_ids":["S314","S316","S317"]},{"text":"Man adalah warga dunia yang rasional, yang tugasnya adalah bertindak sesuai dengan konstitusi alam dan tatanan ilahi (S321, S322). Karakter yang baik adalah tidak menganggap apa pun menguntungkan bagi diri sendiri dan bertindak sesuai peran (S321).","source_ids":["S321"]},{"text":"Kerusakan sejati bagi manusia bukanlah kehilangan harta atau tubuh, melainkan hilangnya karakter (seperti kesopanan atau ketenangan) yang merupakan bagian dari kehendak (will) (S324, S326).","source_ids":["S324","S326"]},{"text":"Filsafat dimulai dari kesadaran akan kelemahan diri dan ketidakmampuan untuk secara sempurna menyesuaikan prasangka bawaan (seperti baik/buruk) dengan kasus nyata. Tujuannya adalah menemukan aturan (kanonos) yang melampaui sekadar 'tampakan' atau 'perasaan' (S330, S333).","source_ids":["S330","S333"]},{"text":"Kecemasan (anxiety) muncul karena manusia menginginkan hal-hal yang berada di luar kekuasaannya (seperti pujian atau kehendak Caesar). Kepercayaan sejati hanya ada dalam penguasaan keadaan internal (keinginan dan keengganannya) (S347, S348).","source_ids":["S347","S348"]},{"text":"Tujuan praktis filsafat adalah menyesuaikan kehendak (will) dengan apa yang terjadi, sehingga seseorang dapat menjalani hidup tanpa ketakutan atau gangguan, baik dalam urusan pribadi maupun sosial (S358, S359).","source_ids":["S358","S359"]},{"text":"Langkah awal dalam filsafat adalah mempelajari providensi Tuhan dan berusaha meniru sifat-sifat ilahi (seperti kesetiaan dan kebebasan) dalam tindakan dan perkataan (S360).","source_ids":["S360"]},{"text":"Membedakan 'menggunakan' dan 'memahami': orang banyak memakai kata baik-buruk seperti buta huruf memakai tulisan atau hewan memakai penampakan. Seseorang yang kaya, punya keluarga dan teman Caesar, tetapi tak tahu apa itu Tuhan, manusia, baik dan jahat — bahkan tak tahu tentang dirinya sendiri. Kebenaran seperti cermin atau dokter: bukan penghinaan, meski orang mengeluh dihina bila dikatakan keinginannya menyala dan opiniannya gegabah.","source_ids":["S361","S362"]},{"text":"Mayoritas manusia seperti hewan di pasar: hanya sibuk dengan 'pakan' (harta, tanah, budak, jabatan). Sedikit yang datang untuk memperhatikan tatanan dunia — siapa yang mengaturnya, apa relasi kita dengan pengatur itu — dan karena itu ditertawakan banyak orang, seperti penonton ditertawakan pedagang di pasar.","source_ids":["S363","S364"]},{"text":"Kekerasan kepalaan pada keputusan bukanlah keteguhan: yang tetap dipegang hanyalah keputusan yang benar, seperti otot yang sehat, bukan kejang orang gila. Contoh teman yang memutuskan mati kelaparan tanpa alasan; jiwa sakit yang menambah keputusan gegabah jadi tak terbantu — 'orang bodoh tak bisa diyakinkan maupun dipecahkan'.","source_ids":["S367","S368","S370"]},{"text":"Baik ada di kemauan, jahat di kemauan, keduanya tidak ada di luar kemauan — tetapi kita tak pernah berlatih memberi jawaban benar di luar sekolah (ketika uang ditunjukkan: uang bukan baik). Rhetorician dan pemain lute gemetar di atas panggung karena tak dilatih tentang pujian dan cemoohan; ketakutan dan kecemasan bukan pekerjaan orang lain. Latihan sejati: takut pada ketakutan itu sendiri, bukan pada kematian atau pengasingan.","source_ids":["S373","S374","S377"]},{"text":"Yang memberatkan kita hanyalah opini: di laut lepas Epictetus sendiri terbayang harus meneguk seluruh laut, padahal tiga pint cukup. Kesedihan perpisahan seperti anak menangis ditinggal pengasuh — orang dewasa juga menangis untuk gimnasium, portikos, air Dirce, Akropolis; perlu 'disapih' ke makanan yang lebih padat. Hukum ilahi: jagakan milikmu, gunakan yang diberikan, serahkan kembali dengan senang hati.","source_ids":["S377","S379","S380","S383"]},{"text":"Membuang kembung diri (self-conceit) adalah tugas pertama filsuf: mustahil belajar apa yang sudah diyakini tahu. Preconception (prolepsis) tentang baik dan sehat sudah kita punya, tetapi tak bisa disesuaikan dengan kasus tanpa analisis dan definisi — sebab itu orang berdebat, seperti dokter terbelah sebelum Hippocrates. Bukti ketidakcocokan: keinginan yang tak terjadi. Medea punya opini benar bahwa keinginan gagal adalah sengsara, tapi salah tahu cara memenuhinya — jangan menginginkan yang di luar kuasa; serahkan desire/aversion kepada para dewa.","source_ids":["S389","S390","S392","S393","S394"]},{"text":"Melawan penampakan lewat kebiasaan: setiap tindakan memperkuat kebiasaannya — marah atau takabur menambah kebiasaan itu seperti menambah bahan bakar api; penyakit jiwa meninggalkan bekas (luka) yang bila tak dihapus total akan kambuh lebih parah. Obatnya: hitung hari tanpa marah, dan saat penampakan datang, tahan dulu — 'tunggu sedikit, biar aku lihat apa kamu' — lalu lawan dengan penampakan yang indah dan mulia. Kemenangan atas penampakan inilah atlet sejati, demi kerajaan, kebebasan, dan ketenangan.","source_ids":["S403","S404","S407","S409"]},{"text":"Kritik pada yang menerima filsafat hanya dalam kata-kata: mengetahui pembagian baik-buruk-indiferen dari Chrysippus atau Cleanthes tidak berbeda dari hafalan sejarah Homer; ujian sejati adalah apakah pembagian itu diingat saat badai di kapal atau saat dipanggil ke pengadilan Caesar. 'Tunjukkan aku seorang Stoik' — orang yang sakit, mati, diasingkan, dan tetap bahagia; bukan sekadar yang mengulang argumen kecil. Sekolah Epictetus bertujuan membuat murid bebas dan bahagia, dan satu-satunya yang dalam kuasa kita adalah penggunaan penampakan yang benar.","source_ids":["S420","S421","S422","S424"]},{"text":"Bantahan terhadap Epicurus dan Akademik: mereka yang menyangkal kebenaran justru memakainya — 'percayalah bahwa tak ada yang perlu dipercaya' adalah kontradiksi. Epicurus menyangkal persaudaraan alami manusia tetapi bangun tidur dan menulis buku untuk memperingatkan orang lain — sifat manusia yang tak terbantahkan memaksanya; seperti tanaman tak bisa tumbuh melawan jenisnya, manusia tak bisa menghapus afeksi kemanusiaan. Doktrin yang merusak kesalehan dan keadilan merusak negara, padahal Sparta dan Thermopylae dibangun dari opini yang sebaliknya.","source_ids":["S428","S429","S431","S434"]},{"text":"Ketidakkonsistenan orang dalam mengakui kesalahan: tak ada yang mengaku bodoh atau tidak adil, tetapi banyak yang mengaku penakut dan penyayang — karena kebingungan tentang baik-buruk; mereka menganggap ketakutan ciri watak baik dan tak mengakui kesalahan terhadap masyarakat.","source_ids":["S440"]},{"text":"Inkonsistensi moral: orang menganggap ketakutan, kasih sayang, cemburu, dan nafsu 'tidak disengaja' untuk membenarkan diri, tetapi ketidakadilan dianggap disengaja. Menghadapi murid yang datang ke sekolah hanya untuk menguasai syllogisme sambil bertengkar dengan budak di rumah; mereka membawa pulang persis yang mereka bawa—teorema tidak berguna bagi yang salah guna, seperti cuka tidak berguna bagi penderita disentri sebelum luka disembuhkan. Alasan mesti dibawa ke sekolah tenang dan bebas distraksi.","source_ids":["S441","S444","S445"]},{"text":"Persahabatan: hanya orang bijak yang mampu mencintai, karena cinta memerlukan pengetahuan tentang Baik. Setiap makhluk terikat pada kepentingannya sendiri; bila kepentingan diletakkan pada hal eksternal, saudara atau ayah pun bisa jadi musuh—seperti anjing yang bertengkar saat sepotong daging dilempar di antara mereka (Eteocles-Polynices, Alexander membakar kuil Aesculapius). Persahabatan sejati ada hanya bila kepentingan diletakkan pada will dan penggunaan penampakan yang benar.","source_ids":["S448","S454","S455"]},{"text":"Uji persahabatan: jangan percaya pada sumpah atau lahir dari orang tua sama—periksa di mana kepentingan orang itu diletakkan (hal luar atau will). 'Kamu menemani saya lama—tahu kamu tidak ia memperlakukanmu seperti membasuh sepatu dengan spons?'; kalung Eriphyle (opini tentang barang) merusak pernikahan Amphiaraus. Yang menempatkan diri pada will akan menjadi teman sejati dan memaafkan yang berbeda karena kebodohan (doktrin Plato: jiwa dirampas kebenaran dengan tak rela).","source_ids":["S456","S458","S459"]},{"text":"Kekuatan berbicara adalah hadiah Tuhan; menyangkalnya tidak syukur dan pengecut. Namun fakultas will adalah yang tertinggi: ia menggunakan semua fakultas lain sebagai pelayan, menilai nilai setiap fakultas, membuka-tutup mata dan telinga; hanya will sendiri yang bisa menghambat will—maka will itulah satu-satunya kebajikan atau kejahatan. Kritik Epicurus yang memposisikan daging sebagai yang terutama padahal daging tidak bisa menulis tentang tujuan hidup.","source_ids":["S462","S464","S466","S467"]},{"text":"Kekuatan bicara dan teorema hanyalah 'penginapan' di jalan pulang: jangan berhenti dan tinggal di sana seperti pelancong yang lupa tujuannya, terpikat pada ungkapan, syllogisme, atau sophisme seperti di antara Sirens. Tujuan sejati: menggunakan penampakan sesuai alam, desire tidak frustrasi, bebas, taat pada administrasi Zeus, tanpa menyalahkan siapa pun ('Lead me, O Zeus, and thou too Destiny'). Bicara seperti Demosthenes atau memecahkan syllogisme seperti Chrysippus tidak mencegah kecelakaan.","source_ids":["S472","S474","S476"]},{"text":"Ada juga seni mendengar: sebagaimana mendengar musik milik musisi dan menilai patung memerlukan seni, mendengar filsuf dengan bermanfaat memerlukan latihan khusus; tidak semua pendengar teruntung—yang mendengar terampil teruntung, yang tidak terampil merugi.","source_ids":["S479","S480"]},{"text":"Kesalahan (error) selalu mengandung kontradiksi: pencuri berpikir mencuri menguntungkan padahal tidak; jiwa rasional tak bisa menyetujui yang palsu bila kefalsahannya tampak. Maka sang pembaharu cukup menunjukkan kontradiksi itu—seperti Socrates yang cukup satu pembicara sebagai saksi—bila tak tampak, saling diri sendiri, bukan orangnya.","source_ids":["S492","S493"]},{"text":"Perawatan diri lewat penampilan (rambut berhias, mencabut bulu) dikritik: keindahan manusia ada pada keunggulan khasnya (keadilan, moderasi, kesederhanaan), bukan pada bagian hewani atau mortalitas; manusia adalah will (proairesis), bukan daging dan rambut. Socrates menasihati Alcibiades untuk menghiasi kemauan dan membuang opini buruk, bukan tubuh.","source_ids":["S496","S497","S508"]},{"text":"Filsuf wajib berkata benar meski pendengar tidak mau dipengaruhi: contoh Apollo tetap berbicara kepada Laius dan Socrates menolak berhenti mengajukan pertanyaan meski diadili; 'aku adalah orang yang bertugas merawat manusia'—yang unggul dalam setiap jenis (seperti ungu pada jubah, bulla melawan singa) tidak perlu membela diri atas keberbedaannya.","source_ids":["S500","S501","S502"]},{"text":"Tiga topik latihan orang yang berprogres: (1) desire/aversion—yang paling utama karena dari situ lahir gejolak; (2) tugas dan relasi alami (anak, ayah, warga) dengan afek yang tidak hampa seperti patung; (3) assent tanpa kekeliruan. Filsuf sezaman menelorkan topik ketiga (sophisme) sambil mengabaikan dua yang pertama—padahal bahkan terganggu oleh ketakutan diremehkan orang.","source_ids":["S512","S513","S514"]},{"text":"Nilai sejati tidak ditunjukkan dengan membaca Chrysippus/Archedemus: Diogenes menunjuk sophist dengan jari tengah—manusia ditunjukkan oleh prinsip-prinsipnya, bukan seperti batu. Yang kapalnya tenggelam tidak waktunya membahas argumen hipotetis; pembahasan logis hanya untuk yang sudah tenang, tanpa marah, duka, dan iri.","source_ids":["S515","S516","S517"]},{"text":"Materi kerja orang baik adalah fakultas penguasanya sendiri: menggunakan penampakan sesuai alam; jiwa tak bisa menolak penampakan baik yang jelas, seperti penukar uang tak bisa menolak koin Caesar—prinsip inilah dasar seluruh gerakan manusia dan Tuhan.","source_ids":["S520"]},{"text":"Baik lebih diutamakan daripada relasi terdekat: tidak ada relasi antara aku dan ayah, tetapi antara aku dan Baik. Bila Baik diletakkan pada penentuan kemauan yang benar, justru pemenuhan relasi hidup menjadi baik; ayah yang mengambil harta tidak melukai — kesopanan dan kesetiaan tak dapat dirampas bahkan oleh Zeus. Setiap orang punya 'koin' sendiri dari Tuhan (proconsul dibayar perak, pezina dengan gadis) yang menentukan apa yang ia beli.","source_ids":["S521","S522"]},{"text":"Latihan harian melawan penampakan: setiap pagi uji setiap penampakan dengan aturan — apakah dalam kuasa kemauan atau tidak; bila tidak, buang ('tidak ada bagimu'). Ratapan, sial, perpecahan sipil, celaan, kekufuran semuanya hanyalah opini tentang hal di luar kemauan seolah baik-buruk; pindahkan opini itu ke hal dalam kemauan maka orang akan teguh. Seperti cahaya di atas air yang bergoyang: jiwa yang terganggu tampak mengacaukan kebajikan, tetapi sebenarnya hanya roh yang perlu dikembalikan tenang.","source_ids":["S523","S524","S525"]},{"text":"Gubernur Epirus yang berseberangan di teater ditegur: banyak orang meniru contoh orang berkuasa; bila berseberangan itu salah, jangan lakukan sendiri; bila benar, jangan marah ditiru. Di teater masuklah dengan tujuan menjaga kemauan sesuai alam — 'tak ada yang lebih kusayang daripada diriku sendiri'; di rumah boleh menggelar permainan sendiri dan menobatkan Sophron, tetapi di publik jangan mengklaim milik semua orang; bila menolak, tanggunglah cemoohan.","source_ids":["S528","S529","S530"]},{"text":"Murid yang ingin pulang karena sakit ditegur: penyakit dan kematian pasti mengejutkan kita saat sedang melakukan sesuatu — berharap dikejutkan saat menjaga kemauan sendiri, agar bisa berkata kepada Tuhan: aku sakit dan miskin karena kehendak-Mu dan tetap pasrah, tak pernah mencela administrasi-Mu. Socrates bahagia karena tiap hari melihat dirinya bertumbuh lebih baik: tak pernah mencela siapa pun, Tuhan maupun manusia, dan selalu berwajah sama.","source_ids":["S533","S534","S537"]},{"text":"Orang baik tak terkalahkan karena tak masuk pertarungan di mana ia lebih lemah: tanah, budak, jabatan, tubuh boleh diambil, tetapi desire dan aversion-nya tak bisa digagalkan — satu-satunya pertarungan yang ia masuki adalah tentang hal dalam kuasa kemauannya. Kemajuan kini terhambat karena akal dilatih untuk memecahkan syllogisme, bukan untuk menjaga fakultas penguasa sesuai alam; jangan mencampur hal yang berbeda.","source_ids":["S540","S541"]},{"text":"Dialog dengan administrator Epicurean: jika daging yang terbaik, maka Maximus berlayar demi daging; tetapi kenikmatan jiwa harus bergantung pada sesuatu yang mendahuluinya — jika bukan hal jiwa, maka hal tubuh, dan substansi Baik jatuh ke tubuh. Konsekuensi logis Epicurean: mencuri dan berzina boleh bila tak terdeteksi — doktrin yang merusak negara dan keluarga. Tugas utama manusia: urusan publik, menikah, membesarkan anak, menghormati Tuhan, merawat orang tua; manusia terbawa bebas, mulia, dan mampu malu — kenikmatan harus jadi pelayan, bukan tuan.","source_ids":["S546","S549","S552","S553"]},{"text":"Kekuasaan menghukum bukan pemerintahan manusia: memenjarakan seperti batu, memukul seperti keledai. Pemerintahan sejati menunjukkan apa yang menguntungkan sebagai makhluk rasional, seperti Socrates. Hukuman bagi yang tak patuh bukan penjara, melainkan kehilangan watak: kesetiaan, kesopanan, kepatutan — jangan cari hukuman lebih besar dari itu.","source_ids":["S554","S555"]},{"text":"Latihan melawan penampakan seperti melawan soal sophistik: anakmu mati — apa yang terjadi? Anakmu mati, tidak lebih; 'ia sengsara' adalah tambahan opini sendiri. Bila menyalahkan Zeus, ingat: ia menjadimu mampu menanggung, menjadimu magnanimous, mengambil kuasa hal-hal menjadi kejahatan, dan membukakan pintu keluar — 'keluarlah dan jangan meratap'.","source_ids":["S558","S559"]},{"text":"Opini adalah sebab segala tindakan: Epictetus tak punya aturan apakah seseorang akan menang di Rome, hanya bahwa dengan opini benar ia berjalan baik. Filsuf yang ditemui hanya sekilas seperti batu bukan pertemuan sejati — bertukar dan menguji opini itulah maknanya. Yang kaya justru lebih miskin: butuh keteguhan, ketenangan, kebebasan dari kecemasan; keinginan yang banyak seperti tangan penuh buah dalam guci leher sempit — buang sebagian agar bisa keluar.","source_ids":["S563","S566","S567","S568"]},{"text":"Sakit adalah bagian hidup seperti berjalan dan berlayar; filosofi adalah persiapan menghadapi peristiwa — menyerah saat demam seperti mundur dari Pancratium setelah dipukul. Menanggung demam dengan baik: tak menyalahkan Tuhan atau manusia, menghadapi kematian dengan mulut, tak gentar atau gembira berlebihan pada kabar dokter. Dua prinsip siap sedia: selain will tak ada baik atau jahat, dan kita harus mengikuti peristiwa, bukan memimpinnya.","source_ids":["S573","S575","S576","S577"]},{"text":"Latihan (exercise) tidak boleh bertentangan dengan alam demi kekaguman (berjalan di tali, memeluk patung) — itu bedahara pesulap. Tujuannya: desire tak frustrasi dan aversion tak jatuh pada yang dihindari; lawan kebiasaan dengan kebiasaan sebaliknya. Pemula harus menjauhi yang lebih kuat darinya (gadis cantik vs pemula filosofi). Tiga topik latihan: desire/aversion, tindakan sesuai alasan, dan assent — periksa setiap penampakan seperti penjaga malam memeriksa izin.","source_ids":["S586","S587","S589","S590"]},{"text":"Kesendirian (solitude) adalah kondisi tak berdaya, bukan sekadar sendiri — bahkan Zeus sendiri di konflagrasi tak menyendiri. Manusia harus mampu jadi teman dirinya sendiri seperti Zeus: memperhatikan administrasi ilahi dan relasi dirinya dengan segala hal. Damai dari Caesar tak melindungi dari demam, kapal karam, cinta, duka; doktrin filosof menjanjikan ketenangan dari semuanya — dan kematian adalah pintu pulang ke unsur-unsur, penuh dewa, bukan Hades.","source_ids":["S594","S595","S596","S597"]},{"text":"Kekuatan besar berbahaya bagi pemula: berlatih menahan diri (makan sedikit, air, menahan desire) agar kelak menginginkan sesuai alasan; berbuat baik lewat contoh hidup, bukan ceramah. Penalti ilahi bagi yang menempatkan baik di luar will: ia akan iri, menyanjung, gelisah; yang menempatkan jahat di luar will akan berduka dan menangis. Setiap relasi (ayah, saudara) diawasi Zeus.","source_ids":["S580","S583","S599"]}],"sources":[{"id":"S601","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"Certain Miscellaneous Matters"},{"id":"S602","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"As bad tragic actors cannot sing alone, but in company with many: so some persons cannot walk about alone. Man, if you are anything, both walk alone and talk to yourself, and do not hide yourself in the chorus. Examine a little at last, look around, stir yourself up, that you may know who you are."},{"id":"S603","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"When a man drinks water, or does anything for the sake of practice (discipline), whenever there is an opportunity he tells it to all: “I drink water.” Is it for this that you drink water, for the purpose of drinking water? Man, if it is good for you to drink, drink; but if not, you are acting ridiculously. But if it is good for you and you do drink, say nothing about it to those who are displeased with water-drinkers. What then, do you wish to please these very men?"},{"id":"S604","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":4,"paragraphEnd":4,"text":"Of things that are done some are done with a final purpose (προηγουμένως), some according to occasion, others with a certain reference to circumstances, others for the purpose of complying with others, and some according to a fixed scheme of life."},{"id":"S605","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":5,"paragraphEnd":5,"text":"You must root out of men these two things: arrogance (pride) and distrust. Arrogance then is the opinion that you want nothing (are deficient in nothing): but distrust is the opinion that you cannot be happy when so many circumstances surround you. Arrogance is removed by confutation; and Socrates was the first who practiced this. And (to know) that the thing is not impossible, inquire and seek. This search will do you no harm; and in a manner this is philosophizing: to seek how it is possible to employ desire and aversion (ἐκκλίσει) without impediment."},{"id":"S606","chapter":"XIV: Certain Miscellaneous Matters","paragraphStart":6,"paragraphEnd":6,"text":"“I am superior to you, for my father is a man of consular rank.” Another says, “I have been a tribune, but you have not.” If we were horses, would you say, “My father was swifter? I have much barley and fodder, or elegant neck ornaments.” If then while you were saying this, I said: Be it so: let us run then. Well, is there nothing in a man such as running in a horse, by which it will be known which is superior and inferior? Is there not modesty (αἰδὼς), fidelity, justice? Show yourself superior in these, that you may be superior as a man. If you tell me that you can kick violently, I also will say to you that you are proud of that which is the act of an ass."},{"id":"S607","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XV"},{"id":"S608","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything"},{"id":"S609","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"In every act consider what precedes and what follows, and then proceed to the act. If you do not consider, you will at first begin with spirit, since you have not thought at all of the things which follow; but afterwards when some consequences have shown themselves, you will basely desist (from that which you have begun). “I wish to conquer at the Olympic games.” [And I too, by the gods: for it is a fine thing]. But consider here what precedes and what follows; and then, if it is for your good, undertake the thing. You must act according to rules, follow strict diet, abstain from delicacies, exercise yourself by compulsion at fixed times, in heat, in cold; drink no cold water, nor wine, when there is opportunity of drinking it. In a word you must surrender yourself to the trainer, as you do to a physician. Next in the contest, you must be covered with sand, sometimes dislocate a hand, sprain an ankle, swallow a quantity of dust, be scourged with the whip; and after undergoing all this, you must sometimes be conquered. After reckoning all these things, if you have still an inclination, go to the athletic practice. If you do not reckon them, observe you will behave like children who "},{"id":"S610","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"at one time play as wrestlers, then as gladiators, then blow a trumpet, then act a tragedy, when they have seen and admired such things. So you also do: you are at one time a wrestler (athlete), then a gladiator, then a philosopher, then a rhetorician; but with your whole soul you are nothing: like the ape you imitate all that you see; and always one thing after another pleases you, but that which becomes familiar displeases you. For you have never undertaken anything after consideration, nor after having explored the whole matter and put it to a strict examination; but you have undertaken it at hazard and with a cold desire. Thus some persons having seen a philosopher and having heard one speak like Euphrates —and yet who can speak like him? —wish to be philosophers themselves."},{"id":"S611","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"Man, consider first what the matter is (which you propose to do), then your own nature also, what it is able to bear. If you are a wrestler, look at your shoulders, your thighs, your loins: for different men are naturally formed for different things. Do you think that, if you do (what you are doing daily), you can be a philosopher? Do you think that you can eat as you do now, drink as you do now, and in the same way be angry and out of humor? You must watch, labor, conquer certain desires, you must depart from your kinsmen, be despised by your slave, laughed at by those who meet you, in everything you must be in an inferior condition, as to magisterial office, in honors, in courts of justice. When you have considered all these things completely, then, if you think proper, approach to philosophy, if you would gain in exchange for these things freedom from perturbations, liberty, tranquillity. If you have not considered these things, do not approach philosophy: do not act like children, at one time a philosopher, then a tax collector, then a rhetorician, then a procurator (officer) of Caesar. These things are not consistent. You must be one man either good or bad: you must either lab"},{"id":"S612","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"or at your own ruling faculty or at external things: you must either labor at things within or at external things: that is, you must either occupy the place of a philosopher or that of one of the vulgar."},{"id":"S613","chapter":"XV: That We Ought to Proceed with Circumspection to Everything","paragraphStart":4,"paragraphEnd":4,"text":"A person said to Rufus when Galba was murdered, “Is the world now governed by Providence?” But Rufus replied, “Did I ever incidentally form an argument from Galba that the world is governed by Providence?”"},{"id":"S614","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XVI"},{"id":"S615","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men"},{"id":"S616","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"If a man has frequent intercourse with others either for talk, or drinking together, or generally for social purposes, he must either become like them, or change them to his own fashion. For if a man places a piece of quenched charcoal close to a piece that is burning, either the quenched charcoal will quench the other, or the burning charcoal will light that which is quenched. Since then the danger is so great, we must cautiously enter into such intimacies with those of the common sort, and remember that it is impossible that a man can keep company with one who is covered with soot without being partaker of the soot himself. For what will you do if a man speaks about gladiators, about horses, about athletes, or what is worse about men? Such a person is bad, such a person is good; this was well done, this was done badly. Further, if he scoff, or ridicule, or show an ill-natured disposition? Is any man among us prepared like a lute-player when he takes a lute, so that as soon as he has touched the strings, he discovers which are discordant, and tunes the instrument? such a power as Socrates had who in all his social intercourse could lead his companions to his own purpose? How shoul"},{"id":"S617","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"d you have this power? It is therefore a necessary consequence that you are carried about by the common kind of people."},{"id":"S618","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"Why then are they more powerful than you? Because they utter these useless words from their real opinions: but you utter your elegant words only from your lips; for this reason they are without strength and dead, and it is nauseous to listen to your exhortations and your miserable virtue, which is talked of everywhere (up and down). In this way the vulgar have the advantage over you: for every opinion (δόγμα) is strong and invincible. Until then the good (κομψαί) sentiments (ὑπολήψεις) are fixed in you, and you shall have acquired a certain power for your security, I advise you to be careful in your association with common persons: if you are not, every day like wax in the sun there will be melted away whatever you inscribe on your minds in the school. Withdraw then yourselves far from the sun so long as you have these waxen sentiments. For this reason also philosophers advise men to leave their native country, because ancient habits distract them and do not allow a beginning to be made of a different habit; nor can we tolerate those who meet us and say: “See such a one is now a philosopher, who was once so-and-so.” Thus also physicians send those who have lingering diseases to a d"},{"id":"S619","chapter":"XVI: That We Ought with Caution to Enter Into Familiar Intercourse with Men","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"ifferent country and a different air; and they do right. Do you also introduce other habits than those which you have: fix your opinions and exercise yourselves in them. But you do not so: you go hence to a spectacle, to a show of gladiators, to a place of exercise (ξυστόν), to a circus; then you come back hither, and again from this place you go to those places, and still the same persons. And there is no pleasing (good) habit, nor attention, nor care about self and observation of this kind: “How shall I use the appearances presented to me? according to nature, or contrary to nature? how do I answer to them? as I ought, or as I ought not? Do I say to those things which are independent of the will, that they do not concern me?” For if you are not yet in this state, fly from your former habits, fly from the common sort, if you intend ever to begin to be something."},{"id":"S620","chapter":"XVII: On Providence","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XVII"},{"id":"S621","chapter":"XVII: On Providence","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"On Providence"},{"id":"S622","chapter":"XVII: On Providence","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"When you make any charge against Providence, consider, and you will learn that the thing has happened according to reason. “Yes, but the unjust man has the advantage.” In what? “In money.” Yes, for he is superior to you in this: that he flatters, is free from shame, and is watchful. What is the wonder? But see if he has the advantage over you in being faithful, in being modest: for you will not find it to be so; but wherein you are superior, there you will find that you have the advantage. And I once said to a man who was vexed because Philostorgus was fortunate: Would you choose to lie with Sura? —“May it never happen,” he replied, “that this day should come?” Why then are you vexed, if he receives something in return for that which he sells; or how can you consider him happy who acquires those things by such means as you abominate; or what wrong does Providence, if he gives the better things to the better men? Is it not better to be modest than to be rich? —He admitted this —Why are you vexed then, man, when you possess the better thing? Remember then always and have in readiness the truth, that this is a law of nature —that the superior has an advantage over the inferior in that"},{"id":"S623","chapter":"XVII: On Providence","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":" in which he is superior —and you will never be vexed."},{"id":"S624","chapter":"XVII: On Providence","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"“But my wife treats me badly.” Well, if any man asks you what this is, say, “my wife treats me badly.” Is there then nothing more? Nothing. —“My father gives me nothing.” —[What is this? my father gives me nothing —Is there nothing else then? —Nothing]: but to say that this is an evil is something which must be added to it externally, and falsely added. For this reason we must not get rid of poverty, but of the opinion about poverty, and then we shall be happy."},{"id":"S625","chapter":"XVIII: That We Ought Not to Be Disturbed by Any News","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XVIII"},{"id":"S626","chapter":"XVIII: That We Ought Not to Be Disturbed by Any News","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"That We Ought Not to Be Disturbed by Any News"},{"id":"S627","chapter":"XVIII: That We Ought Not to Be Disturbed by Any News","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"When anything shall be reported to you which is of a nature to disturb, have this principle in readiness: that the news is about nothing which is within the power of your will. Can any man report to you that you have formed a bad opinion, or had a bad desire? By no means. But perhaps he will report that some person is dead. What then is that to you? He may report that some person speaks ill of you. What then is that to you? Or that your father is planning something or other. Against whom? Against your will (προαίρεσις)? How can he? But is it against your poor body, against your little property? You are quite safe: it is not against you. But the judge declares that you have committed an act of impiety. And did not the judges (δίκασται) make the same declaration against Socrates? Does it concern you that the judge has made this declaration? No. Why then do you trouble yourself any longer about it? Your father has a certain duty, and if he shall not fulfil it, he loses the character of a father, of a man of natural affection, of gentleness. Do not wish him to lose anything else on this account. For never does a man do wrong in one thing, and suffer in another. On the other side it is "},{"id":"S628","chapter":"XVIII: That We Ought Not to Be Disturbed by Any News","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"your duty to make your defense firmly, modestly, without anger: but if you do not, you also lose the character of a son, of a man of modest behavior, of generous character. Well then, is the judge free from danger? No; but he also is in equal danger. Why then are you still afraid of his decision? What have you to do with that which is another man’s evil? It is your own evil to make a bad defense: be on your guard against this only. But to be condemned or not to be condemned, as that is the act of another person, so it is the evil of another person. A certain person threatens you. Me? No. He blames you. Let him see how he manages his own affairs. He is going to condemn you unjustly. He is a wretched man."},{"id":"S629","chapter":"XIX: What Is the Condition of a Common Kind of Man and of a Philosopher","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XIX"},{"id":"S630","chapter":"XIX: What Is the Condition of a Common Kind of Man and of a Philosopher","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"What Is the Condition of a Common Kind of Man and of a Philosopher"},{"id":"S631","chapter":"XIX: What Is the Condition of a Common Kind of Man and of a Philosopher","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"The first difference between a common person (ἰδιώτης) and a philosopher is this: the common person says, “Woe to me for my little child, for my brother, for my father.” The philosopher, if he shall ever be compelled to say, “Woe to me,” stops and says, “but for myself.” For nothing which is independent of the will can hinder or damage the will, and the will can only hinder or damage itself. If then we ourselves incline in this direction, so as, when we are unlucky, to blame ourselves and to remember that nothing else is the cause of perturbation or loss of tranquillity except our own opinion, I swear to you by all the gods that we have made progress. But in the present state of affairs we have gone another way from the beginning. For example, while we were still children, the nurse, if we ever stumbled through want of care, did not chide us, but would beat the stone. But what did the stone do? Ought the stone to have moved on account of your child’s folly? Again, if we find nothing to eat on coming out of the bath, the pedagogue never checks our appetite, but he flogs the cook. Man, did we make you the pedagogue of the cook and not of the child? Correct the child; improve him. In "},{"id":"S632","chapter":"XIX: What Is the Condition of a Common Kind of Man and of a Philosopher","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"this way even when we are grown up we are like children. For he who is unmusical is a child in music; he who is without letters is a child in learning: he who is untaught, is a child in life."},{"id":"S633","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XX"},{"id":"S634","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":1,"paragraphEnd":1,"text":"That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things"},{"id":"S635","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"In the case of appearances which are objects of the vision, nearly all have allowed the good and the evil to be in ourselves, and not in externals. No one gives the name of good to the fact that it is day, nor bad to the fact that it is night, nor the name of the greatest evil to the opinion that three are four. But what do men say? They say that knowledge is good, and that error is bad; so that even in respect to falsehood itself there is a good result, the knowledge that it is falsehood. So it ought to be in life also. Is health a good thing, and is sickness a bad thing? No, man. But what is it? To be healthy, and healthy in a right way, is good: to be healthy in a bad way is bad; so that it is possible to gain advantage even from sickness, I declare. For is it not possible to gain advantage even from death, and is it not possible to gain advantage from mutilation? Do you think that Menoeceus gained little by death? Could a man who says so, gain so much as Menoeceus gained? Come, man, did he not maintain the character of being a lover of his country, a man of great mind, faithful, generous? And if he had continued to live, would he not have lost all these things? would he not hav"},{"id":"S636","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":2,"paragraphEnd":2,"text":"e gained the opposite? would he not have gained the name of coward, ignoble, a hater of his country, a man who feared death? Well, do you think that he gained little by dying? I suppose not. But did the father of Admetus gain much by prolonging his life so ignobly and miserably? Did he not die afterwards? Cease, I adjure you by the gods, to admire material things. Cease to make yourselves slaves, first of things, then, on account of things, slaves of those who are able to give them or take them away."},{"id":"S637","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"Can advantage then be derived from these things? From all; and from him who abuses you. Wherein does the man who exercises before the combat profit the athlete? Very greatly. This man becomes my exerciser before the combat: he exercises me in endurance, in keeping my temper, in mildness. You say no: but he, who lays hold of my neck and disciplines my loins and shoulders, does me good; and the exercise master (the aliptes, or oiler) does right when he says: Raise him up with both hands, and the heavier he (ἐκεῖνος) is, so much the more is my advantage. But if a man exercises me in keeping my temper, does he not do me good? —This is not knowing how to gain an advantage from men. Is my neighbour bad? Bad to himself, but good to me: he exercises my good disposition, my moderation. Is my father bad? Bad to himself, but to me good. This is the rod of Hermes: touch with it what you please, as the saying is, and it will be of gold. I say not so: but bring what you please, and I will make it good. Bring disease, bring death, bring poverty, bring abuse, bring trial on capital charges: all these things through the rod of Hermes shall be made profitable. “What will you do with death?” Why, wha"},{"id":"S638","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":3,"paragraphEnd":3,"text":"t else than that it shall do you honor, or that it shall show you by act through it, what a man is who follows the will of nature? “What will you do with disease?” I will show its nature, I will be conspicuous in it, I will be firm, I will be happy, I will not flatter the physician, I will not wish to die. “What else do you seek?” Whatever you shall give me, I will make it happy, fortunate, honored, a thing which a man shall seek."},{"id":"S639","chapter":"XX: That We Can Derive Advantage from All External Things","paragraphStart":4,"paragraphEnd":4,"text":"You say “No: but take care that you do not fall sick: it is a bad thing.” This is the same as if you should say, “Take care that you never receive the impression (appearance) that three are four: that is bad.” Man, how is it bad? If I think about it as I ought, how shall it then do me any damage? and shall it not even do me good? If then I think about poverty as I ought to do, about disease, about not having office, is not that enough for me? will it not be an advantage? How then ought I any longer to look to seek evil and good in externals? What happens? these doctrines are maintained here, but no man carries them away home; but immediately everyone is at war with his slave, with his neighbours, with those who have sneered at him, with those who have ridiculed him. Good luck to Lesbius, who daily proves that I know nothing."},{"id":"S640","chapter":"XXI: Against Those Who Readily Come to the Profession of Sophists","paragraphStart":0,"paragraphEnd":0,"text":"XXI"}],"newWindowIds":["S601","S602","S603","S604","S605","S606","S607","S608","S609","S610","S611","S612","S613","S614","S615","S616","S617","S618","S619","S620","S621","S622","S623","S624","S625","S626","S627","S628","S629","S630","S631","S632","S633","S634","S635","S636","S637","S638","S639","S640"]}
requests.raw: {"notes":[{"text":"Lakukan segala tindakan dengan pertimbangan matang: pertimbangkan apa yang mendahului dan mengikuti, seperti atlet Olimpiade harus menerima latihan ketat, diet, dan kekalahan. Tanpa pertimbangan manusia seperti anak kecil atau kera yang meniru apa saja — kadang atlet, kadang gladiator, kadang filsuf — tanpa pernah satu hal pun dikerjakan dengan seluruh jiwa; harus memilih jadi satu orang: filosof atau orang biasa.","source_ids":["S609","S610","S611"]},{"text":"Pilih lingkungan pergaulan dengan hati-hati: bila bersosialisasi, kita pasti menyerupai orang lain atau mengubah mereka — seperti arang padam dekat arang menyala. Pendapat orang biasa kuat karena keluar dari keyakinan sungguhan, sementara exhortasi filosofis kita hanya kata-kata 'dari bibir' yang mati; hingga prinsip baik menjadi teguh, jauhi kebiasaan lama dan pergaulan umum, bahkan meninggalkan kampung halaman seperti dokter mengirim pasien ke udara berbeda.","source_ids":["S616","S618","S619"]},{"text":"Tentang providence: tidak perlu terganggu bila orang tidak adil 'menang' dalam uang — unggul di sana karena tanpa malu dan suciapapun; hukum alam: yang lebih unggul unggul dalam hal kemampuannya sendiri. Jangan katakan 'kekasihku memperlakukanku buruk adalah kejahatan' — cukup laporkan fakta; yang perlu dibuang bukan kemiskinan melainkan opini tentang kemiskinan.","source_ids":["S622","S624"]},{"text":"Berita yang mengganggu selalu tentang hal di luar will: tak ada yang bisa melaporkan bahwa kamu beropini buruk atau menginginkan hal buruk. Pemakzulan hakim terhadap Socrates tak menyentuh dirinya; kejahatan hakim adalah milik hakim — tangkiskanlah dengan pembelaan yang tegas dan sopan tanpa marah.","source_ids":["S627","S628"]},{"text":"Perbedaan utama orang biasa vs filosof: orang biasa berkata 'dedih aku karena anakku', filosof berkata 'dedih aku karena diriku sendiri' — sebab hanya will yang bisa merusak will. Kita terbiasa sejak kecil menyalahkan batu (dipukul pengasuh) atau koki, padahal harusnya anak yang dikoreksi; yang tak terlatih adalah anak dalam hidup.","source_ids":["S631","S632"]},{"text":"Keuntungan bisa diperoleh dari segala hal luar, bahkan dari yang menghina: orang jahat baginya sendiri, bagiku ia 'pemukul latihan' yang melatih ketahanan dan kesabaran — tongkat Hermes yang mengubah apa saja jadi emas: bawa penyakit, kematian, kemiskinan, dan aku jadikan semuanya terhormat. Menoeceus memperoleh banyak dengan mati mempertahankan cinta tanah air.","source_ids":["S635","S637","S638"]}]}
